works.title: The Myth of Sisyphus
works.author: Albert Camus
works.description: This Is A Standalone Non-Fiction Collection Of Philosophical Essays That Examines Existentialist Thought, The Search For Meaning In A Universe Without Inherent Order, And The Possibility Of Living With Dignity And Authenticity. Designed For Adult Readers, Students Of Philosophy, And Anyone Curious About How To Confront Despair With Purpose, The Tone Is Thoughtful, Serious, And Hopeful. The Essays Are Presented In Clear, Accessible Prose That Guides Readers Through Core Questions About Existence, Meaning, And Responsibility. It Offers A Rigorous Yet Readable Path Into Existentialist Ideas, With A Standalone Edition Designed For Easy Study Or Discussion. Reading This Collection Is A Contemplative Experience, Blending Precise Argument With Lyrical Insight. Readers Are Invited To Reflect, Connect The Ideas To Their Own Lives, And Consider What It Means To Live With Dignity, Courage, And Authenticity In A Complex World. Core Themes: Meaning, Freedom, Responsibility, Authenticity In A World Without Inherent Order Accessible Prose: Lucid, Precise, And Lyrical Writing That Invites Careful Reading Standalone Edition: Convenient For Independent Study Or Group Discussion Reader Engagement: Prompts Thoughtful Reflection On Personal Values And Daily Choices After Finishing, Readers Gain A Framework For Approaching Life’S Big Questions With Courage, Curiosity, And Resilience. It Offers A Fresh Perspective On Personal Meaning And Leaves A Lasting Impression Of Clarity And Renewed Purpose.
works.authorDescription:
Albert Camus ( kam-OO; French: [albɛʁ kamy] ; 7 November 1913 – 4 January 1960) was a French philosopher, writer, and political activist. He was the recipient of the 1957 Nobel Prize in Literature at the age of 44, the second-youngest recipient in history, and the first laureate in literature born in Africa. His works include The Stranger, The Plague, The Myth of Sisyphus, The Fall and The Rebel.
Camus was born in French Algeria to pied-noir parents. He spent his childhood in a poor neighbourhood and later studied philosophy at the University of Algiers. He was in Paris when the Germans invaded France during World War II in 1940. Camus tried to flee but finally joined the French Resistance where he served as editor-in-chief at Combat, an outlawed newspaper. After the war, he was a celebrity figure and gave many lectures around the world. He married twice but had many extramarital affairs. Camus was politically active; he was part of the left that opposed Joseph Stalin and the Soviet Un...

works.title: Games People Play
works.author: Eric Berne
works.description: Since Its Publication Over 5 Million Copies Have Been Sold Worldwide In Over Ten Languages , And Spent More Than Two Years On The New York Times Bestseller List When It Was First Released Eric Berne Was A Prominent Psychiatrist And Bestselling Author.After Inventing His Groundbreaking Transactional Analysis, He Continued To Develop And Apply This New Methodology Leading Him To Publish Games People Play. This Became A Runaway Success And Berne Leaves A Remarkable Legacy Of Over 30 Other Books And Articles, As Well As The Founding Of The International Transactional Analysis Association. Dr Berne's Other Works Include Principles Of Group Treatment, A Layman's Guide To Psychiatry And Psychoanalysis', And What Do You Say After You Say Hello? He Died In 1970. 'if You're Going To Read One Psychology Book In Your Lifetime It Should Be This One' - Amazon Review ' A Brilliant, Amusing And Clear Catalogue Of The Psychological Theatricals That Human Beings Play Over And Over Again ' Kurt Vonnegut, Author Of Cat's Cradle And Slaughterhouse Five The Bestselling Classic On How To Harness The Rules Of Human Behaviour To Make The Most Of Your Work, Relationships And Life Fed Up Of Feeling Controlled At Work? Feel Trapped In A Toxic Relationship But Don't Know How To Escape? Always Feel Like You Lose The Argument Even If You Know Deep Down You're Right? Widely Recognised As The Most Original And Influential Psychology Book Of Our Time, Games People Play Has Helped Millions Of People Better Understand Human Basic Social Interactions And Relationships. We Play Games All The Time: Relationship Games; Power Games With Our Bosses And Competitive Games With Our Friends. In This Book, Berne Reveals The Secret Ploys And Manoeuvres That Rule Our Lives And How To Combat Them. Giving You The Keys To Unlock The Psychology Of Others And Yourself, This Classic, Entertaining And Life-Changing Book Will Open Up The Door To Honest Communication And Teach You How To Get The Most Out Of Life. ' An Extraordinary Set Of Ideas That Are Still Useful In Our World Today' - Amazon Review
works.authorDescription:
Eric Berne (May 10, 1910 – July 15, 1970) was a Canadian-born psychiatrist who created the theory of transactional analysis as a way of explaining human behavior.
Berne's theory of transactional analysis was based on the ideas of Freud and Carl Jung but was distinctly different. Freudian psychotherapists focused on talk therapy as a way of gaining insight to their patient's personalities. Berne believed that insight could be better discovered by analyzing patients' social transactions.

works.title: Essentialism
works.author: Greg McKeown
works.description: A disciplined approach to doing less but better, focusing time and energy solely on tasks that are truly essential.
works.authorDescription: Greg McKeown is an author and public speaker who writes about leadership and strategy, originating from the UK and based in California.

works.title: An American Marriage
works.author: Tayari Jones
works.description: An American Marriage is a novel by the American author Tayari Jones. It is her fourth novel and was published by Algonquin Books on February 6, 2018. In February 2018, the novel was chosen for Oprah's Book Club 2.0. The novel also won the 2019 Women's Prize for Fiction.
works.authorDescription: Tayari Jones (born November 30, 1970) is an American author and academic known for An American Marriage, which was a 2018 Oprah's Book Club Selection and won the 2019 Women's Prize for Fiction. Jones is a graduate of Spelman College, the University of Iowa, and Arizona State University. She is currently a member of the English faculty in the College of Arts and Sciences at Emory University and recently returned to her hometown of Atlanta after a decade in New York City. Jones was Andrew Dickson White Professor-at-large at Cornell University before becoming Charles Howard Candler Professor of Creative Writing at Emory University.

works.title: Light from Many Lamps
works.author: Lillian Eichler Watson
works.description: A Classic Treasury Of Inspiration Featuring Hundreds Of Passages And Quotations—Selected From The Wisdom Of The Ages—Offering Invaluable Insight And Guidance On The Challenges Of Daily Life. Here Are Not Only The Best Of The World’S Most Inspiring Thoughts And Ideas, But The Stories Behind Them: How They Came To Be Written And What Their Impact Has Been On Others. A Storehouse Of Inspired And Inspiring Reading, It Is A Collection Of Brief, Stimulating Biographies As Well. There Are Selections From John Burroughs, Alfred Tennyson, Robert Browning, Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Abraham Lincoln, Franklin D. Roosevelt, William Cullen Bryant, Ralph Waldo Emerson, William Shakespeare, Hippocrates, Confucius, And Many Others. A Distillation Of The Greatest Thoughts, Ideas, And Philosophies That Have Been Handed Down To Us Through The Ages, This Is A Book To Turn To Over And Over Again—A Book Of Moral, Spiritual, And Ethical Guidance—An Unfailing Source Of Comfort And Inspiration For All.
works.authorDescription:
Lillian Eichler Watson (April 3, 1901 – June 25, 1979) was an American advertising copywriter and author of bestselling books of etiquette. Her first Book of Etiquette, published in 1921 and for which she created the advertising campaign Again She Orders..."A Chicken Salad, Please", was an immediate bestseller and was followed by several updated volumes and numerous other books.
Many of Eichler's ad campaigns targeted social anxiety.

works.title: Awara Bheed ke Khatre
works.author: Harishankar Parsai
works.description: A sharp, satirical essay collection critiquing the herd mentality, corruption, and social decay in modern Indian society.
works.authorDescription: Harishankar Parsai was a noted Hindi writer and satirist who won the Sahitya Akademi Award for revolutionizing Hindi satire.

works.title: Areba Pareba
works.author: Uday Prakash
works.description: मैंने एक नहीं, कई तरह की कहानियाँ लिखी हैं। कई-कई रूपों, शिल्प-शैलियों, संरचनाओं और आकारों की कहानियाँ। कुछ कहानियाँ बहुत लम्बी हैं- लगभग उपन्यास की सरहद को छूती हुई। कुछ आलोचक (उनसे कैसे बचा जा सकता है?) इन्हें कहानियाँ मानने से इनकार करते हुए, उन्हें ‘नॉवेला’ (लघु उपन्यास) घोषित करते हैं। ‘पीली छतरी वाली लड़की’, ‘वारेन हेस्टिंग्स का साँड़’ या ‘...और अन्त में प्रार्थना’ ऐसे ही लम्बे आख्यान हैं। लेकिन मैं यह अच्छी तरह जानता हूँ कि इन रचनाओं का गठन, इनका विन्यास और इनकी आन्तरिक संरचना उपन्यास की तरह नहीं है। साधारण प्रचलित कहानियों के मुकाबले कई बार लगभग दस गुना लम्बी ये कहानियाँ इतने पृष्ठों के विस्तार के बावजूद अपनी गति और आवयविक बनावट में अन्ततः कहानियाँ ही हैं, ‘लघु’ या ‘दीर्घ’ उपन्यास नहीं। मैं हिन्दी ही नहीं, अन्य भाषाओं के पाठकों का भी हृदय से आभारी हूँ जिन्होंने आख्यान के इलाके में मेरे कई आकस्मिक प्रयोगों और दुस्साहसिकताओं को समूची आत्मीयता से अपनाया और स्वीकार किया। ”उदय प्रकाश की रचनाओं पर विचार करते समय हमेशा अन्याय होता है। तारीफ़ भी ग़लत की जाती रही है। उनके लेखन की वास्तविक पहचान यदि हो जाये, तो एक पूरी धारा टूट जाये। वे कथा-साहित्य का रचनात्मक विकल्प खोजने वाले महत्त्वपूर्ण कथाकार हैं।” -मुद्राराक्षस “उदय प्रकाश समाज के हाशिए में जीने वाले लोगों के कहानीकार हैं। वे समाज की विद्रूपताओं को बेनकाब करते हैं। समर्थों द्वारा असमर्थों को दबाने-कुचलने के षड्यन्त्रों की पोल खोलते हैं। उनकी कहानियों में एक प्रयोग है, डिबिया में बन्द धूप के टुकड़े की सी मासूमियत है, किशोर मन का सपना है अजाने सुख को स्पर्श करने का, युवा भावों की कोमलता है, साथ ही अभाव का, कुछ छूट जाने का, कुछ न पाने की कमी का अहसास है, ज़िन्दगी का यथार्थ है। उदय प्रकाश सम्भवतः इस पीढ़ी के सर्वश्रेष्ठ कथाकार हैं, न सिर्फ़ हिन्दी में, बल्कि सभी भारतीय भाषाओं में....” -प्रसन्ना, रंगकर्मी एवं एक्टिविस्ट
works.authorDescription:
Uday Prakash (born 1 January 1952) is a Hindi poet, scholar, journalist, translator and short story writer from India.
He has worked as administrator, editor, researcher, and TV director. He writes for major dailies and periodicals as a freelancer. He has also received several awards for his collection of short stories and poems. With Mohan Das he received Sahitya Academi Awards in 2011. He is the first author to return his Sahitya Akademi award on September 3, 2015 against the killing of M. M. Kalburgi that initiated a storm of national protests by writers, artists, scholars and intellectuals.

works.title: Man Up
works.author: Bedros Keuilian
works.description: "But I can't . . ." "There's no way . . ." "It's impossible . . ." Enough. Get off your ass and make your "someday" goals a priority—today. After years of coaching and consulting hundreds of startup rookies as well as seasoned entrepreneurs, executives, and CEOs, Bedros Keuilian realized that most people who want to start a business, grow an existing business, author a book, make more money, or make a bigger impact usually take the long, slow, painful way to get there . . . and more than 80 percent of entrepreneurs never get to their desired destination or achieve their full potential in business. They treat their dream as if it were merely a hobby and dip their toes in the water, but they never commit to diving in—you get the idea. It's time to cut the bullshit excuses. Everyone has a gift, a purpose. It's your duty to figure out what your gift is and how you're going to share it with the world. Man Up: How to Cut the Bullshit and Kick Ass in Business (and in Life) is your guide to doing exactly that. Keuilian, founder and CEO of Fit Body Boot Camp and known as the "hidden genius" behind many of the most successful brands and businesses throughout multiple industries, will show you how to break out of the sea of mediocrity, get singularly focused on your purpose, and do what it takes—not only to achieve but dominate your goals. With Keuilian's no-nonsense approach in both business and personal spheres, you'll be able to define your purpose and have clarity of vision—and a plan—to make the quantum leap. Whether it's creating and growing a company, leaving a legacy, making a difference, or launching a new brand, you will discover how to use your passion, purpose, and sheer grit to overcome any adversity that attempts to derail your progress. If there's an area of your life in which you need to man up, this book will get you there.

works.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
works.author: Eric Jorgenson
works.description: GETTING RICH IS NOT JUST ABOUT LUCK; HAPPINESS IS NOT JUST A TRAIT WE ARE BORN WITH. These aspirations may seem out of reach, but building wealth and being happy are skills we can learn. So what are these skills, and how do we learn them? What are the principles that should guide our efforts? What does progress really look like? Naval Ravikant is an entrepreneur, philosopher, and investor who has captivated the world with his principles for building wealth and creating long-term happiness. The Almanack of Naval Ravikant is a collection of Naval's wisdom and experience from the last ten years, shared as a curation of his most insightful interviews and poignant reflections. This isn't a how-to book, or a step-by-step gimmick. Instead, through Naval's own words, you will learn how to walk your own unique path toward a happier, wealthier life.

works.title: Indistractable
works.author: Nir Eyal
works.description: "Indistractable provides a framework that will deliver the focus you need to get results." —James Clear, author of Atomic Habits "If you value your time, your focus, or your relationships, this book is essential reading. I'm putting these ideas into practice." —Jonathan Haidt, author of The Righteous Mind NATIONAL BESTSELLER WINNER OF THE OUTSTANDING WORKS OF LITERATURE (OWL) AWARD INCLUDED IN THE TOP 5 BEST PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT BOOKS OF THE YEAR BY AUDIBLE INCLUDED IN THE TOP 20 BEST BUSINESS AND LEADERSHIP BOOKS OF THE YEAR BY AMAZON FEATURED IN THE AMAZON BOOK REVIEW NEWSLETTER, JANUARY 2020 GOODREADS BEST SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY OF 2019 FINALIST You sit down at your desk to work on an important project, but a notification on your phone interrupts your morning. Later, as you're about to get back to work, a colleague taps you on the shoulder to chat. At home, screens get in the way of quality time with your family. Another day goes by, and once again, your most important personal and professional goals are put on hold. What would be possible if you followed through on your best intentions? What could you accomplish if you could stay focused? What if you had the power to become "indistractable?" International bestselling author, former Stanford lecturer, and behavioral design expert, Nir Eyal, wrote Silicon Valley's handbook for making technology habit-forming. Five years after publishing Hooked, Eyal reveals distraction's Achilles' heel in his groundbreaking new book. In Indistractable, Eyal reveals the hidden psychology driving us to distraction. He describes why solving the problem is not as simple as swearing off our devices: Abstinence is impractical and often makes us want more. Eyal lays bare the secret of finally doing what you say you will do with a four-step, research-backed model. Indistractable reveals the key to getting the best out of technology, without letting it get the best of us. Inside, Eyal overturns conventional wisdom and reveals: • Why distraction at work is a symptom of a dysfunctional company culture—and how to fix it • What really drives human behavior and why "time management is pain management" • Why your relationships (and your sex life) depend on you becoming indistractable • How to raise indistractable children in an increasingly distracting world Empowering and optimistic, Indistractable provides practical, novel techniques to control your time and attention—helping you live the life you really want.

works.title: Same as Ever
works.author: Morgan Housel
works.description: The New York Times and Sunday Times bestseller. As featured on the Dr Chatterjee podcast Feel Better, Live More and the Diary of a CEO podcast with Steven Bartlett. From the author of the multi-million copy selling The Psychology of Money. Same As Ever will arm you with a powerful new ability to think about risk and opportunity, and navigate the uncertainty of the future. When planning for the future, we often ask something like, “What will the economy be doing this time next year?” Or we want to know, “What will be different ten years from now?” But forecasting is hard. The important events that will shape the future are inherently unpredictable. Instead, we should be asking a different question: What will be the same in the future as it is now? Knowledge of the things that never change is more useful, and more important, than an uncertain prediction of an unknowable future. In Same As Ever, bestselling author Morgan Housel shares 24 short stories about the ways that life, behaviour, and business will always be the same. As you see familiar themes repeat again and again in the years ahead, you’ll find yourself nodding and saying, “Yep, same as ever.” With this new knowledge and confidence, you will be on the path to living a good life.

works.title: Freakonomics
works.author: Levitt & Dubner
works.description: Freakonomics Is A Groundbreaking Exploration Of Economics That Asks Why People Make The Choices They Do, From Crime To Parenting To Education. Co-Authored By Steven Levitt And Stephen J. Dubner, This Speaks To Curious Readers Of All Backgrounds, Offering Witty, Accessible Insights That Feel Surprising Yet Obvious In Hindsight. Structured As A Collection Of Engaging Essays, Freakonomics Dives Into Real-World Questions With A Data-Driven But Human Storytelling Approach. Each Chapter Applies Economic Thinking To Unexpected Topics, Weaving Anecdotes, Studies, And Thoughtful Analysis Into A Narrative That Invites Readers To Reconsider What They Think They Know. The Experience Is Lively And Accessible—The Pace Is Brisk, The Stakes Feel Personal, And The Ideas Stick Because They Illuminate Hidden Incentives Behind Everyday Outcomes. If You’Re New To Economics, You’Ll Find Concepts Like Incentives, Information, And Cause-And-Effect Explained In Practical Terms, While Seasoned Readers Will Appreciate The Clever Connections And Provocative Angles. The Book’S Strength Lies In Its Ability To Make Complex Ideas Feel Obvious And Relevant, Turning Dry Theories Into Compelling Stories About Crime, Education, Parenting, Sports, And More. Broad Range Of Topics Examined Through An Economic Lens, From Crime To Education To Parenting To Sports Engaging, Narrative-Driven Writing That Blends Data, Case Studies, And Memorable Anecdotes Clear Explanations Of Core Concepts Like Incentives, Information Asymmetry, And Unintended Consequences Short, Approachable Chapters That Invite Reflection And Curiosity Without Heavy Jargon Edition Designed For Comfortable Reading And Easy Reference After Finishing Freakonomics , Readers Gain A Sharper Habit Of Questioning Assumptions And Spotting The Hidden Forces Shaping Daily Life. The Book Leaves You Thinking Differently About Choices, Consequences, And The World Around You, Offering Lasting Insights You’Ll Carry Into Conversations, Decisions, And Policy-Minded Thinking.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Brave New World
works.author: Aldous Huxley
works.description: A dystopian novel depicting a genetically engineered futuristic society built on constant pleasure, consumerism, and the loss of individual freedom.
works.authorDescription: Aldous Huxley was an English writer and philosopher who wrote nearly fifty books and is celebrated as one of the preeminent intellectuals of his time.

works.title: Crucial Conversations
works.author: Patterson et al.
works.description: One of the best books on personal development related to improving interpersonal skills. This book teaches how to handle that critical one to one communication that has the potential to sabotage ones relationship if not handled carefully. How unbeknownst to us our own heart betrays us when we get caught up in heat of argument and subconsciously plans, hatches up plan to defeat our intentions this book explains it all. Book offers principles, know how & practices to develop self-awareness during those critical moment when conversation can spiral out of control from innocent to crucial to disastrous. Book is guided by serious research of tools offered. Examples provided to illustrate are to the point & extremely persuasive. One can have immediate impact on ones life if one becomes aware of basic principles presented even one is not in possession of skills required or yet to acquire the skills to practice those principles.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: The Outsiders
works.author: William Thorndike
works.description: This is a powerful young adult fiction title that follows a fourteen-year-old narrator and his friends as they navigate loyalty, class divisions, and the pull between bravado and vulnerability. Set on the tough streets of a mid-sized American town, it is a gritty, emotionally honest coming-of-age story designed to resonate with readers who crave character-driven drama. The tone is raw but hopeful, blending tension with empathy. It’s a YA classic that invites readers to reflect on what loyalty really means, what it costs to stand up for friends, and how a single moment can change a life forever. The narrative is story-led and tightly paced, with vivid dialogue and cinematic scenes that pull you into a world shaped by tough choices and close friendships. Readers experience the tension through a clear, accessible voice and a grounded sense of place that makes the stakes feel personal. As the reader follows the protagonist through challenge after challenge, the story asks big questions about belonging, courage, and the line between protection and violence. The reading experience is immersive, prompting reflection without heavy-handed messaging. Compelling teenage protagonist voice that feels immediate and authentic Explores loyalty, class differences, identity, and resilience Fast-paced, dialogue-driven storytelling with vivid, cinematic moments Film-era cultural impact and status as a long-standing coming-of-age classic Accessible, engaging narrative that invites readers to think about consequences and choices Readers finish with a deeper understanding of belonging, the costs of violence, and the strength found in friendship. The story leaves a lasting impression that sparks curiosity, empathy, and a more nuanced view of adolescence and society.
works.authorDescription: William Thorndike was a Massachusetts lawyer and politician who served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives, and as a member and President of the Massachusetts Senate.

works.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
works.author: Philip K. Dick
works.description: A science fiction novel following a bounty hunter tasked with 'retiring' rogue androids on a post-apocalyptic Earth; the basis for Blade Runner.
works.authorDescription: Philip K. Dick was an American science fiction writer whose works deeply explored reality, identity, and authoritarianism.

works.title: The Things They Carried
works.author: Tim O'Brien
works.description: A collection of linked, semi-autobiographical short stories about a platoon of American soldiers fighting in the Vietnam War.
works.authorDescription: Tim O'Brien is an American novelist and veteran whose writing focuses heavily on the American experience in the Vietnam War.

works.title: Born a Crime
works.author: Trevor Noah
works.description: It's Trevor Noah Born A Crime - Is A Young Readers' Adaptation Of Trevor Noah's Bestselling Memoir, Born A Crime: Stories From A South African Childhood. This Remarkable True Story Follows A Boy Growing Up Mixed Race In South Africa During And After Apartheid, Told With Warmth, Humor, And Resilience. Written For Curious Readers Who Love Real-Life Stories With Heart, This Book Offers An Inspiring, Educational, And Hopeful Journey That Matters To Anyone Who Cares About Identity, Family, And Overcoming Obstacles. The Book Is Written In Accessible, Story-Driven Prose That Feels Like Listening To A Trusted Friend. Short Chapters, Vivid Scenes, And A Warm, Engaging Voice Carry Readers Through A Difficult History With Grace And Humor, While Staying True To The Seriousness Of The Moments. Trevor Noah’S Journey—From Mischievous Boy To Thoughtful Young Man—Unfolds With Candor And Heart, Inviting Readers To Laugh, Reflect, And Grow Along The Way. It Also Presents Key Concepts—Identity, Family, Resilience, And The Power Of Humor To Cope With Adversity—Through Relatable Moments And Cultural Context. In It's Trevor Noah Born A Crime - , The Storytelling Approach Makes History Accessible: Clear Turns Of Phrase, Everyday Scenes, And A Steady Pace That Encourages Empathy, Curiosity, And A Sense Of Possibility. Personal, True-Life Story Of Trevor Noah's Childhood Under Apartheid And Beyond Accessible, Story-Driven Prose Crafted For Young Readers Themes Of Identity, Family, Resilience, And Humor That Empower Growth Short Chapters And Vivid Scenes Create A Warm, Engaging Reading Rhythm Connections To A Major Motion Picture Adaptation Starring Lupita Nyong'o After Finishing It's Trevor Noah Born A Crime - , Readers Gain A Deeper Understanding Of Resilience, Identity, And The Role Humor Plays In Overcoming Obstacles. This Book Leaves Them Feeling Inspired, Curious About The World, And Confident That One Voice—Steeped In Courage And Laughter—Can Help Shape A Brighter Future.
works.authorDescription: Trevor Noah is a South African comedian, writer, producer, political commentator, actor, and television host. He was the host of The Daily Show, an American late-night talk show and satirical news program on Comedy Central, from 2015 to 2022. Noah has won various awards, including two Primetime Emmy Awards. He was named one of "The 35 Most Powerful People in New York Media" by The Hollywood Reporter in 2017 and 2018. In 2018, Time magazine named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world.

works.title: Blink
works.author: Malcolm Gladwell
works.description: An exploration of intuition and 'thin-slicing'—how humans make split-second decisions that are often more accurate than carefully analyzed choices.
works.authorDescription: Malcolm Gladwell is a Canadian journalist, staff writer for The New Yorker, and bestselling author known for his pop-sociology books.

works.title: Digital Fortress
works.author: Dan Brown
works.description: Digital Fortress Is A High-Stakes Techno-Thriller Set Inside The National Security Agency, Where A Mysterious, Seemingly Unbreakable Code Triggers A Tense Race Against Time. Written For Adult Readers Who Love Fast-Paced Espionage, Intricate Puzzles, And Political Intrigue, This Gripping Tale Blends Danger With Intellect And Keeps You Turning Pages. Through Tight, Action-Forward Chapters, Digital Fortress Follows Susan Fletcher, The Nsa’S Chief Cryptographer, As She Discovers That The Code’S Power Extends Far Beyond A Simple Cipher. The Narrative Hops From Fort Meade To The Sunlit Streets Of Seville, Weaving Technical Intrigue With Human Drama And A Web Of Risk, Secrecy, And Shifting Loyalties. Ensei Tankado, The Enigmatic Creator Of The Code, Adds A Chilling Personal Dimension To The Chase. The Storytelling Feels Brisk But Smart, Inviting Readers To Track Clues, Weigh Choices, And Feel The Clock Tick In Real Time. Intricate Code And Cryptography At The Heart Of The Mystery A Globe-Spanning Chase From Fort Meade To Seville Cinematic, Propulsive Pacing With Clear, Accessible Prose Rich Themes Of Secrecy, Power, Trust, And Ethical Crosscurrents Memorable Characters And A Tense, Believable Atmosphere Of National Security After Finishing Digital Fortress, Readers Gain A Sharper Sense Of How Information Can Shape Nations And How Courage And Trust Must Navigate Risk. The Book Leaves You Contemplating Power, Responsibility, And The Human Costs Of Security, All While Delivering A Pulse-Pounding Thrill That Lingers Long After The Last Page.
works.authorDescription: Daniel Gerhard Brown is an American writer best known for his thriller novels, particularly the Robert Langdon series Angels & Demons (2000), The Da Vinci Code (2003), The Lost Symbol (2009), Inferno (2013), Origin (2017) and The Secret of Secrets (2025). His novels are treasure hunts that usually take place over a 24-hour period and center on recurring themes of cryptography, art, and conspiracy theories.

works.title: Urdu-Hindi Shabdkosh
works.author: Mohd. Mustafa Khan
works.description: This Is Not A Conventional Dictionary, But A Curated Anthology Of Carefully Selected Urdu Poetic Words Shabdon Complete With Compelling Couplets And Detailed Explanations. The Book Explores: The Artistic Use Of Poetic Vocabulary In Urdu— Origins And Influences From Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit, And Turkish Word‑Meanings, Connotations, And Talmīḥāt Literary Allusions/References The Nuances Of Usage, Context In Different Themes, And Exploring The Emotional Depth Behind Common Poetic Terms If You're Passionate About Urdu Poetry And Wish To Deepen Your Understanding Of Its Rich Lexicon And Expressive Breadth, This Volume Offers An Immersive And Enlightening Companion.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Lean In
works.author: Sheryl Sandberg & Nell Scovell
works.description: 100 Delicious Recipes And A Plan For Sustainable Fat Loss From Instagram Star, Joe Wicks. The Opposite Of The Unenjoyable Low Calorie Crash Diets, Lean In 15 Showcases Delicious Recipes And A Plan For Sustainable Fat Loss That Will Inspire Busy People To Keep Their Body Healthy And Lean Forever. Featuring 100 Healthy And Quick To Prepare Meals As Well As Including Examples Of His Signature Hiit High Intensity Interval Training Home Workouts, Lean In 15 Enables You To Achieve Incredible Fat Loss And Build A Fit, Strong And Lean Body.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Clear Thinking
works.author: Shane Parrish
works.description: Clear Thinking — Offers A Practical, Mindset-Shifting Guide To Decision-Making In A Noisy World. Grounded In Insightful Conversations With Some Of The Brightest Minds In Entrepreneurship And Decision-Making, This Book Helps You Cut Through Clutter And Cultivate A Clear, Confident Mindset. If You’Re An Adult Reader Seeking Smarter Choices At Work, At Home, And In Daily Life, Clear Thinking Speaks Directly To You With An Inspiring, Educational, And Empowering Tone. Shane Parrish Guides You Through A Structured, Reader-Friendly Approach That Blends Concise Explanations With Real-World Conversations. The Book Is Built Around Practical Frameworks And Bite-Sized Lessons; Each Chapter Distills A Key Concept And Shows How To Apply It, With Lively Storytelling And Concrete Examples From Entrepreneurship And Decision-Making. You’Ll Discover How To Spot Cognitive Biases, Test Assumptions, And Design Decisions That Align With Your Goals, All At A Pace That’S Approachable And Engaging. As A Non-Fiction Guide, Clear Thinking Presents Ideas In A Way That’S Easy To Grasp And Easy To Put Into Practice. The Content Is Presented Through Practical Examples And Actionable Strategies That You Can Apply Day By Day, Turning Theory Into Habits. The Writing Is Clear And Encouraging, Making Complex Topics Feel Accessible And Even Enjoyable As You Move Toward Smarter Choices In Everyday Life. Key Content Elements: Decision-Making Frameworks, Cognitive Biases, Practical Examples Standout Features: Bite-Sized Lessons And Real-World Scenarios Learning Outcomes: Sharper Thinking And Better, More Confident Decisions Writing Style: Clear, Engaging, Accessible Prose After Finishing Clear Thinking, You’Ll Have A Practical Toolkit For More Intentional Choices, A Calmer, More Focused Mindset, And The Confidence To Navigate Uncertainty With Clarity. This Book Helps You Think Differently—Less Overwhelmed, More Purposeful—And Stays With You As A Reliable Companion On Your Journey Toward Smarter Decisions.
works.authorDescription: Shane Parrish is a fictional character from the Australian soap opera Home and Away, played by Dieter Brummer. He made his first on-screen appearance on 28 May 1992 and he departed on 13 March 1996.

works.title: Homeland Elegies
works.author: Ayad Akhtar
works.description: In 'Homeland Elegies,' Ayad Akhtar intricately weaves a deeply personal narrative exploring hope and identity within a fractured nation
works.authorDescription: Ayad Akhtar is an American playwright, novelist, and screenwriter. He has received numerous accolades including the 2013 Pulitzer Prize for Drama as well as nominations for two Tony Awards.

works.title: Made to Stick
works.author: Chip & Dan Heath
works.description: Made to Stick: Why Some Ideas Survive and Others Die is a book by brothers Chip and Dan Heath published by Random House on January 2, 2007. The book expands upon the idea of 'stickiness' popularized by Malcolm Gladwell in The Tipping Point, seeking to explain what makes an idea or concept memorable or interesting
works.authorDescription: Chip Heath is a professor at Stanford Graduate School of Business, and Dan Heath is a senior fellow at Duke University's CASE center.

works.title: The Great Mental Models
works.author: Shane Parrish
works.description: This non-fiction guide offers a practical toolkit of mental models—clear, reusable concepts drawn from science and everyday observation that help you see how the world works, make sharper decisions, and boost your productivity. It’s written for curious readers, professionals, students, and leaders who want to think more clearly and act with confidence. The content is presented as concise explanations of core models, illustrated with real-world examples from business, science, and daily life. Concepts are introduced in plain language, with short takeaways and relatable prompts that invite you to try them out. Readers build a latticework of ideas you can reference at work, at home, and in any decision you face, turning theory into tangible results. Concepts covered include how small forces can produce large effects (leverage), why momentum matters (inertia), and what it takes to spark change (activation energy). You’ll also encounter ideas like opportunity costs, feedback loops, and first principles thinking. The language is accessible, with practical, bite-sized executions that make learning feel natural and enjoyable. Core models and how to apply them across contexts, from daily decisions to strategic planning Learning outcomes focused on improved decision making, faster information synthesis, and stronger pattern recognition Clear explanations, real-world examples, and concise takeaways that you can reuse immediately Practical prompts, checklists, and reflective questions to integrate new thinking into your routine After finishing, readers gain a reusable framework for clearer thinking, better problem solving, and renewed curiosity about how the world works. It builds confidence to tackle complex information, invites ongoing learning, and leaves a thoughtful, lasting impression on how you approach every decision.
works.authorDescription: Shane Parrish is a fictional character from the Australian soap opera Home and Away, played by Dieter Brummer. He made his first on-screen appearance on 28 May 1992 and he departed on 13 March 1996.

works.title: Beloved
works.author: Toni Morrison
works.description: It is the mid-1800s. At Sweet Home in Kentuckhy, an era is ending as slavery comes under attack from the abolitionists. The worlds of Halle and Paul D. are to be destroyed in a cataclysm of torment and agony. The world of Sethe, however, is to turn from one of love to one of violence and death - the death of Sethes baby daughter Beloved, whose name is the single word on the tombstone, who died at her mothers hands, and who will return to claim retribution.**One of the BBC’s 100 Novels That Shaped Our World**
works.authorDescription: Chloe Anthony Wofford "Toni" Morrison was an American novelist and editor. She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993. Her first novel, The Bluest Eye, was published in 1970. The critically acclaimed Song of Solomon (1977) brought her national attention and won the National Book Critics Circle Award. In 1988, Morrison won the Pulitzer Prize for Beloved (1987). Some of her other notable works include Sula (1973) and Recitatif (1983).

works.title: Abundance
works.author: Klein & Thompson
works.description: An essay/book project exploring how the central challenge of the modern economy is supply and the logistics of building a better future.
works.authorDescription: Ezra Klein and Derek Thompson are prominent American journalists and podcast hosts focusing on economics, politics, and technology.

works.title: Gandhi aur Saraladevi Chaudhrani
works.author: Alka Saraogi
works.description: A historical novel exploring the intense, complex, and little-known relationship between Mahatma Gandhi and Saraladevi Chaudhrani.
works.authorDescription: Alka Saraogi is a Sahitya Akademi Award-winning Indian novelist who writes in Hindi and focuses on historical and social narratives.

works.title: Factfulness
works.author: Hans Rosling
works.description: Factfulness Is A Clear, Data-Driven Journey Into How We Understand The World. This Nonfiction Guide Explores Global Trends With A Hopeful, Can-Do Tone And Invites Readers—Especially Curious Adults And Students—To Examine Facts Rather Than Fear. If You Want A Wiser, More Confident Approach To Current Events, This Book Matters Because It Helps You Think Clearly And Compassionately About Progress. Factfulness Is Written By Hans Rosling, With Ola Rosling And Anna Rosling Rönnlund, Structured As Approachable Chapters That Pair Questions With Data-Led Explanations. The Book Invites Readers To Test Their Assumptions Through Simple, Real-World Examples And Accessible Visuals, Turning Statistics Into A Narrative You Can Follow Without Getting Lost In Jargon. The Pacing Is Thoughtful And Calm, Making The Experience Enjoyable As It Reveals How Our Instincts Can Mislead Us And How Facts Can Reshape Our Worldview. Whether You Read It Cover To Cover Or Dip Into Topics As Needed, Factfulness Presents Key Ideas Like Cognitive Biases, Data Literacy, And The Importance Of Tracking Progress Over Time. The Presentation Blends Storytelling With Clear Charts And Relatable Case Studies, Making Learning Feel Natural And Engaging Rather Than Dry. It’S A Practical Companion For Anyone Who Wants To Think More Accurately About Health, Education, Poverty, And Other Global Trends. Key Content Elements: Bias Exploration, Data-Driven Insights, Global Trends, Progress Across Health, Education, And Poverty. Interactive Or Standout Features: Thought-Provoking Questions And Accessible Visuals That Bring Data To Life. Learning Outcomes Or Experiences: Improved Critical Thinking, Better Ability To Evaluate Information, And A More Confident Worldview. Writing Or Illustration Style: Clear, Conversational, Reader-Friendly Data Storytelling. After Finishing Factfulness, You Gain A Sharpened Ability To Distinguish Fact From Rumor, A More Balanced View Of Global Progress, And The Confidence To Engage With Information Thoughtfully. It Leaves Readers Feeling Hopeful, Informed, And Ready To Carry Evidence-Based Thinking Into Everyday Decisions.
works.authorDescription: Hans Rosling was a Swedish physician, academic, and public speaker. He was a professor of international health at Karolinska Institute and was the co-founder and chairman of the Gapminder Foundation, which developed the Trendalyzer software system. Widely regarded as one of the most influential physicians and geographers in the modern world, he held presentations around the world, including several TED Talks in which he promoted the use of data to explore development issues. His posthumously published book Factfulness, coauthored with his daughter-in-law Anna Rosling Rönnlund and son Ola Rosling, became an international bestseller.

works.title: Never Let Me Go
works.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
works.description: Never Let Me Go is a 2005 science fiction novel by the British author Kazuo Ishiguro. It was shortlisted for the 2005 Man Booker Prize, for the 2006 Arthur C. Clarke Award and the 2005 National Book Critics Circle Award. Time magazine named it the best novel of 2005.
works.authorDescription: Sir Kazuo Ishiguro  is a Japanese-British novelist, screenwriter, musician, and short-story writer. He is one of the most critically acclaimed contemporary fiction authors writing in English, having been awarded several major literary prizes, including the 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature. In its citation, the Swedish Academy described Ishiguro as a writer "who, in novels of great emotional force, has uncovered the abyss beneath our illusory sense of connection with the world".

works.title: Models
works.author: Mark Manson
works.description: "You can become irresistibly attractive to women without changing who you are." So says Mark Manson, superstar blogger and author of the international bestseller, The Subtle Art of Not Giving A F*ck, a self help book that packs a punch. Mark brings the same approach to teaching men what they need to know about attracting women. In Models he shows us how much it sucks trying to attract women using the tricks and tactics recommended by other books. Instead, he says, men need to focus on seduction as an emotional process not a physical or social one. What matters is the intention, the motivation, the authenticity. To improve your dating life you must improve your emotional life - how you feel about yourself and how you express yourself to others. Funny, irreverent and confronting, Models is a mature and honest guide on how a man can attract women by giving up the bullsh*t and becoming an honest broker."A detailed guide to modern sexual ethics" Sydney Morning Herald"There's nothing subtle about Mark Manson. He's crude and vulgar and doesn't give a f*ck . . . He's as painfully honest as he is outrageously funny" Huffington Post

works.title: Outwitting the Devil
works.author: Napoleon Hill
works.description: Napoleon Hill, who was one of America’s greatest influential thinkers, reveals how you can triumph over obstacles to find success in business and in life in his classic book, Outwitting the Devil, profound, powerful, resonant, and rich with insight. The Devil ensnares and controls our minds so we are unable to achieve our personal goals. Hill went so far as to interview the Devil, himself, exploring the innermost depths of the psychology of motivation to understand why so many individuals, including himself, let fear, procrastination, anger and jealousy prevent us from realizing our full potential. The resulting confession from the Devil made this book so controversial as to remain unpublished for over 70 years. The good news is that it is available to you now! Not only is it an insightful and revolutionary perspective on human growth, but with the study guide included in this Deluxe Special Edition, it serves as a powerful hands-on toolkit to achieving personal victory. As you journey through the book and accompanying study guide, you are taken through a step-by-step personal development process that will assist you in conquering your own “inner” demons. You can explore and move beyond your own personal beliefs, fears, blocks and programming and ultimately be released from self-destructive behaviors. With his legendary ability to get to the root of human potential, Napoleon Hill lays out the exact nature of the power by which the Devil disarms human beings. This is the same power that paralyzed millions of individuals with fear and despondency during the Great Depression and continues to hold people back from their dreams. By opening our minds to acquire knowledge that might not seem to mesh with our personal beliefs, we can access a greater truth that will “bring harmony out of chaos in this age of frustration and fear.” Learn the seven principles to freedom that Hill details in this book and move beyond them on your own introspective journey, so you can finally overcome the causes of failure and misery. It’s time to eliminate your destructive habits, and unlock the secret to outwitting the devil once and for all.

works.title: Wild at Heart
works.author: John Eldredge
works.description: A CBA Bestseller A Publishers Weekly Bestseller An ECPA Gold Medallion WinnerIn his heart, every man longs for a battle to fight, an adventure to live, and a beauty to rescue. Now John Eldredge invites men to recover their masculine heart, defined in the image of a passionate God, and women to discover the secret of a man's soul and to delight in the strength and wildness men were created to offer.

works.title: The Effective Executive
works.author: Peter Drucker
works.description: The measure of the executive, Peter Drucker reminds us, is the ability to 'get the right things done'. Usually this involves doing what other people have overlooked, as well as avoiding what is unproductive. He identifies five talents as essential to effectiveness, and these can be learned; in fact, they must be learned just as scales must be mastered by every piano student regardless of his natural gifts. Intelligence, imagination and knowledge may all be wasted in an executive job without the acquired habits of mind that convert these into results. One of the talents is the management of time. Another is choosing what to contribute to the particular organization. A third is knowing where and how to apply your strength to best effect. Fourth is setting up the right priorities. And all of them must be knitted together by effective decision-making. How these can be developed forms the main body of the book. The author ranges widely through the annals of business and government to demonstrate the distinctive skill of the executive. He turns familiar experience upside down to see it in new perspective. The book is full of surprises, with its fresh insights into old and seemingly trite situations.

works.title: A Brief History of Time
works.author: Stephen Hawking
works.description: This is a children’s science picture book that brings cosmology to life through vivid illustrations and clear explanations. Its central theme is time, space, and the universe, guiding curious readers to understand how the cosmos began, what stars and galaxies are, and how scientists describe gravity and time. The intended reader includes curious kids and families, roughly ages 8–12, with an emotional tone of wonder, clarity, and inspiring curiosity. Content is presented as a visually driven journey through space, with over 150 color illustrations and captions designed to illuminate complex ideas. The book traces ideas from classical theories to modern cosmology, covering the Big Bang, space-time, black holes, spiral galaxies, and evolving theories. The reading experience is distinctive because images and succinct explanations work together on every spread, helping readers build mental models while staying engaged. In this gift edition, a newly added appendix provides updates to ideas and tributes to the field’s history. This non-fiction educational resource introduces foundational concepts in cosmology and physics in approachable terms. Concepts covered include the Big Bang, gravity, space-time, black holes, galaxies, and how scientists test ideas. Learning feels accessible and enjoyable thanks to clear language, structured explanations, and abundant visuals that translate abstract ideas into concrete images. Rich, color illustrations (over 150) with captions that clarify core ideas Visual journey through foundational physics and cosmology: gravity, space-time, Big Bang, black holes, and galaxies Gift edition with updated appendix and tributes to the field’s history Clear, friendly prose and reader-friendly layout designed for early readers and curious minds Diagrams and guided progression that invite readers to make connections and deepen understanding After finishing, readers gain a grounded understanding of the universe, enhanced curiosity, and a lasting sense of wonder that invites further exploration of science and learning.
works.authorDescription:
Stephen William Hawking (8 January 1942 – 14 March 2018) was an English theoretical astrophysicist, cosmologist, and author who was director of research at the Centre for Theoretical Cosmology at the University of Cambridge. Between 1979 and 2009, he was the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge, widely viewed as one of the most prestigious academic posts in the world.
Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians. In 1959, at the age of 17, he began his university education at University College, Oxford, where he received a first-class BA degree in physics. In 1962, he began his graduate work at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, where, in 1966, he obtained his PhD in applied mathematics and theoretical physics, specialising in general relativity and cosmology. In 1963, at age 21, Hawking was diagnosed with an early-onset slow-progressing form of motor neurone disease that gradually, over decades, paralysed him. After the loss of his speech, he communicated through a speech-ge...

works.title: Atomic Habits
works.author: James Clear
works.description: Atomic Habits Is A Practical Guide To Lasting Change That Shows How Tiny, Consistent Actions Compound Into Extraordinary Results. Part Self-Help, Part Psychology, This Book Helps You Rethink Goals And Harness The Power Of Small Daily Habits. Suitable For Adults And Curious Readers Who Want More Productivity, Motivation, And Well-Being, Its Warm, Encouraging Tone Makes Complicated Ideas Feel Accessible. In Atomic Habits , James Clear Breaks The Core Idea Into Clear, Actionable Steps. The Book Explains How Tiny Changes—1 Percent Improvements—Daily Can Rewrite Your Trajectory And Shows You How To Build Effective Routines, Design Your Environment, And Leverage Strategies Like Habit Stacking And The Two Minute Rule. Written In A Warm, Accessible Voice With Real-World Stories From Olympic Athletes, Successful Ceos, And Scientists, It Blends Cutting-Edge Psychology With Practical Guidance So The Path To Change Feels Doable Rather Than Daunting. Core Idea: Tiny Daily Improvements Compound Into Big Life Changes. Practical Strategies: Habit Stacking, The Two Minute Rule, And Environment Design. Real-World Examples: Stories From Olympic Athletes, Ceos, And Scientists. Clear, Straightforward Writing That Makes Concepts Easy To Adopt. Learning Outcomes: Improved Productivity, Motivation, Well-Being, And More Effective Routines. With Atomic Habits As Your Guide, You Gain A Practical Blueprint To Reshape Daily Life, Feel More In Control, And Sustain Momentum Toward Long-Term Goals. It Leaves You Inspired To Act, See Small Steps As Powerful, And Carry A Lasting Sense Of Confidence Into Everyday Decisions.
works.authorDescription: James Clear (born January 22, 1986) is an American writer. Raised in Hamilton, Ohio, and receiving education from Denison University and Ohio State University, he is best known for his 2018 self-help book Atomic Habits.

works.description: A psychiatrist's look at the modern world's addiction to instant gratification and how to find balance in a culture of excess.

works.title: Meditations
works.author: Marcus Aurelius
works.description: This non-fiction philosophy book gathers timeless reflections on how we think, feel, and act in daily life. Rooted in ancient wisdom, it guides readers toward calm judgment, resilience, and virtuous leadership. Ideal for adults and curious minds seeking practical philosophy, the tone is thoughtful, steady, and uplifting. The work supports interactive learning through reflective study and practical application. The content unfolds as concise, meditative passages framed by a leadership-focused arc. Short sections invite quiet reading and personal interpretation, encouraging readers to pause, apply the insights to real-life choices, and revisit them as needed. The narrative approach makes timeless ideas feel relevant to modern concerns and everyday decisions. Concepts covered include emotional regulation, self-judgment, discipline, gratitude, and ethical leadership. The accessible language and universal themes make dense ideas approachable and actionable, with gentle prompts that invite reflection and personal growth. Concise, contemplative passages on mind, emotion, and conduct Core concepts: emotional regulation, self-judgment, discipline, gratitude, leadership Narrative framing by a renowned ancient ruler provides a steady, trustworthy voice Clear, accessible language that translates philosophy into daily practice Encourages reflective thinking and personal application to real-life situations Supports interactive learning and activity-based learning through contemplation Readers finish with practical tools for navigating life’s challenges with resilience and virtue, a calmer perspective, and renewed curiosity about human nature and leadership. The insights linger, shaping daily choices and broadening outlook for years to come.
works.authorDescription:
Marcus Aurelius Antoninus ( or-EE-lee-əs; Latin: [ˈmaːrkʊs au̯ˈreːli.us antoːˈniːnʊs]; 26 April 121 – 17 March 180) was Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic philosopher. He was a member of the Nerva–Antonine dynasty, the last of the rulers later known as the Five Good Emperors and the last emperor of the Pax Romana, an age of relative peace, calm, and stability for the Roman Empire lasting from 27 BC to 180 AD. He served as Roman consul in 140, 145, and 161.
Marcus Aurelius was the son of the praetor Marcus Annius Verus and his wife Domitia Calvilla. He was related through marriage to the emperors Trajan and Hadrian. Marcus was three when his father died, and he was raised by his mother and paternal grandfather. After Hadrian's adoptive son, Aelius Caesar, died in 138, Hadrian adopted Marcus's uncle Antoninus Pius as his new heir. In turn, Antoninus adopted Marcus and Lucius, the son of Aelius. Hadrian died that year, and Antoninus became emperor. Now heir to the throne, Marcus st...

works.title: Deep Work
works.author: Cal Newport
works.description: Deep Work: Rules For Focused Success In A Distracted World Is A Practical Guide To Reclaiming Focus And Boosting Productivity. Part Self-Help, Part Performance Manual, The Book Shows How Deep Concentration Can Drive Extraordinary Results In Any Field. It Speaks To Professionals, Students, And Lifelong Learners Who Want To Do Meaningful Work More Efficiently, And The Tone Is Encouraging, Respectful, And Empowering. Written In A Clear, Conversational Voice, Deep Work Blends Research, Real-World Examples, And Actionable Guidance Into A Structured Approach. Newport Explains How To Carve Out Uninterrupted Time, Shape Your Workday Around Deep Tasks, And Build Habits That Protect Attention. The Experience Feels Like A Focused Coaching Session—Practical, Readable, And Designed To Fit Even The Busiest Schedules. Key Concepts Covered Include Minimizing Digital Noise, Scheduling Deep Work Sessions, And Pushing Back Against Shallow Tasks. With Solid Scientific Backing And Accessible Explanations, The Book Translates Theory Into Habits You Can Start Today, Helping You Produce Higher-Quality Work In Less Time And With Greater Satisfaction. Core Ideas: Deep Work, Attention Management, Reducing Shallow Tasks Practical Strategies: Routines And Time Blocks To Protect Focus Evidence-Based Approach: Research-Backed Concepts And Real-World Examples Learning Outcomes: Higher-Quality Work In Less Time, Stronger Focus, Greater Confidence Writing Style: Clear, Practical, And Approachable After Finishing Deep Work, Readers Will Carry A Practical Plan To Protect Their Attention, Produce Meaningful Work With Greater Efficiency, And Move Through Their Days With More Focus And Purpose.
works.authorDescription: Calvin C. Newport is an American nonfiction author and full-time professor of computer science at Georgetown University. He is known for his writings about attention management in the digital age.

works.title: Sri Lanka: The New Country
works.author: Padma Rao Sundarji
works.description: The thirty-year-long civil war in Sri Lanka which ended in 2009 shook the island-nation. Now there is peace, rapid development - and a new government. But questions remain. What do Tamils and Sinhalese feel about their new country?
works.authorDescription: Padma Rao Sundarji a.k.a. Padma Rao is an Indian author and an international correspondent based in New Delhi, India.

works.title: Mendeleyev's Dream
works.author: Paul Strathern
works.description: A narrative history of chemistry charting the journey from ancient alchemy to the creation of the periodic table of elements.
works.authorDescription: Paul Strathern is a Scottish writer and academic known for his books on the history of science and philosophy.

works.title: Mindset
works.author: Carol Dweck
works.description: Mindset Is A Transformative Exploration Of How Our Beliefs Shape Talent And Achievement. In This Groundbreaking Non-Fiction Work, Psychologist Carol Dweck Reveals The Difference Between Fixed And Growth Mindsets And Shows How Adopting A Growth Mindset Can Boost Learning, Resilience, And Success. Mindset Is Ideal For Parents, Teachers, Coaches, Students, And Professionals Seeking Practical, Science-Based Strategies To Nurture Potential And Lifelong Curiosity. The Tone Is Hopeful, Encouraging, And Educational. Written With Clarity And Grounded In Decades Of Research, Mindset Guides Readers Through The Core Idea That Intelligence And Talent Are Not Fixed Traits. It Contrasts The Fixed Mindset With The Growth Mindset And Explains How Praise For Innate Ability Can Hinder Long-Term Achievement. The Book Blends Accessible Theory With Real-World Examples—From Classrooms To Boardrooms—And Offers Practical Steps You Can Apply Right Away To Encourage Effort, Strategies, And Resilience. Structured To Be Engaging And Actionable, Mindset Uses A Mix Of Stories, Data, And Bite-Sized Lessons To Help Readers Implement Change. Whether You’Re A Parent Shaping A Child’S Mindset, A Teacher Guiding A Classroom, A Manager Building High-Performing Teams, Or An Athlete Chasing Peak Performance, The Book Provides Clear Tools For Fostering A Culture Of Learning. Expect Memorable Concepts, Checklists, And Strategies Designed To Help You Nurture Growth In Yourself And Others. Core Concepts: Fixed Vs Growth Mindset And Their Impact On Achievement Practical Strategies: Feedback That Fosters Learning, Shifting Praise, And Goal-Setting Audience And Applicability: Parents, Teachers, Coaches, And Leaders Learning Outcomes: Resilience, Motivation, And A Love Of Learning Accessible, Research-Backed Style: Engaging Storytelling Backed By Evidence After Finishing Mindset, Readers Carry A Clear Framework For Approaching Challenges With Curiosity And Resilience, Cultivating A Lifelong Love Of Learning. This New Perspective Helps You Think Differently About Talent And Success And Empowers You To Pursue Growth In All Areas Of Life.
works.authorDescription: Carol Susan Dweck (born October 17, 1946) is an American psychologist. She holds the Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professorship of Psychology at Stanford University. Dweck is known for her work on motivation and mindset. She was on the faculty at the University of Illinois, Harvard, and Columbia before joining the Stanford University faculty in 2004. She was named an Association for Psychological Science (APS) James McKeen Cattell Fellow in 2013, an APS Mentor Awardee in 2019, and an APS William James Fellow in 2020, and has been a member of the National Academy of Sciences since 2012.

works.title: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits
works.author: Philip Fisher
works.description: A classic investment book emphasizing long-term growth investing and analyzing a company's management and potential.
works.authorDescription: Philip Fisher was an American stock investor and author, widely considered a pioneer of growth investing.

works.title: The Winner Effect
works.author: Ian Robertson
works.description: What makes a winner? Why do some people succeed both in life and in business, and others fail? Why do a few individuals end up supremely powerful, while many remain powerless? The 'winner effect' is a term used in biology to describe how an animal that has won a few fights against weak opponents is much more likely to win later bouts against stronger contenders. As Ian Robertson reveals, it applies to humans, too. Success changes the chemistry of the brain, making you more focused, smarter, more confident, and more aggressive. The effect is as strong as any drug. And the more you win, the more you will go on to win. But the downside is that winning can become physically addictive.By understanding what the mental and physical changes are that take place in the brain of a 'winner,' how they happen, and why they affect some people more than others, Robertson answers the question of why some people attain and then handle success better than others. He explains what makes a winner—or a loser—and how we can use the answers to these questions to understand better the behavior of our business colleagues, family, friends, and ourselves.

works.title: Everything Is F*cked
works.author: Mark Manson
works.description: Everything Is F*Cked Is A Provocative, Accessible Examination Of Why, Even In A World Of Abundance, Many People Feel Adrift. Part Philosophy, Part Social Critique, This Book Speaks To Adults And Curious Readers Who Wrestle With Meaning In A Noisy, Fast-Moving Age. The Tone Is Candid, Brave, And Hopeful, Inviting You To Confront Uncomfortable Truths With Humor And Heart. Everything Is F*Cked Unfolds As A Sequence Of Essays And Reflections That Brush Against Philosophy—From Plato To Nietzsche—While Staying Rooted In Contemporary Life. Manson Writes With Clarity And Punch, Weaving Personal Stories With Big Ideas To Explain Why Modern Success Often Coexists With Emotional Fatigue. The Book Challenges Readers To Consider How Technology, Media, Money, And Entertainment Shape What They Value, And To Rethink Where True Happiness Might Lie. In A Warm, Conversational Voice, The Book Guides You Through Chapters That Unfold With A Brisk, Accessible Pace. It Blends Provocative Insights With Practical Takeaways, Making The Exploration Feel Doable Rather Than Overwhelming. Whether You Read For Ideas, Reassurance, Or A New Approach To Daily Life, This Work Offers A Refreshing Perspective On Finding Meaning Amid Chaos. Explores The Paradox Of Wealth And Emotional Well-Being Accessible, Candid Writing That Blends Philosophy, Psychology, And Culture Thought-Provoking Essays On Technology, Money, Entertainment, And Meaning Insights Into The Intersections Of Religion, Politics, And Modern Life Engaging Storytelling With Relatable Anecdotes And A Brisk, Inviting Pace After Finishing Everything Is F*Cked, Readers Gain A Clearer Sense Of What Matters And How To Live With Intention In An Uncertain World—Feeling More Hopeful, Resilient, And Ready To Navigate The Noise With A Grounded, Personal Compass.
works.authorDescription:
Mark Manson  (born March 9, 1984) is an American self-help author and blogger.
As of 2026, he has authored or co-authored four books, three of which, The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck, Everything Is F*cked: A Book About Hope, and Will, were New York Times bestsellers.

works.title: The 5 AM Club
works.author: Robin Sharma
works.description: Unlock The Power Of The Dawn With The 5 Am Club – Own Your Morning, A Transformative Blend Of Storytelling And Practical Guidance. From Leadership And Performance Expert Robin Sharma, This Book Follows Two Strangers Mentored By An Eccentric Tycoon As They Uncover How Rising Early Can Unlock Extraordinary Focus, Energy, And Fulfillment. Designed For Adults And Anyone Seeking A Proven Path To Higher Productivity, Greater Clarity, And Lasting Momentum, This Book Offers An Inspiring, Hopeful, And Actionable Invitation To Change. Written As A Vivid Narrative, The 5 Am Club – Own Your Morning Blends Scenes, Dialogue, And Practical Lessons Into A Cohesive Guide. The Story-Led Approach Is Paired With A Clear, Step-By-Step Morning Routine That Protects The Quiet Hours Of Dawn, Leaving Space For Exercise, Self-Renewal, And Personal Growth. The Experience Is Engaging And Accessible, With Concise Explanations, Practical Prompts, And A Pace That Stays Firmly Grounded In Real-Life Application. If You’Re Seeking Concrete Takeaways, The Book Delivers Neuroscience-Backed Practices That Explain Why Waking Early Fuels Creativity And Decision-Making, Not Just Willpower. You’Ll Encounter Exclusive Strategies To Shield Your Talents And Dreams From Digital Distractions And Trivial Diversions, Turning Mornings Into A Launchpad For Influence, Impact, And Meaningful Progress. The Reader Will Witness How Top Leaders Begin Their Days, And You’Ll Be Invited To Apply The Same Principles At A Pace That Fits Your Life. A Narrative Following Two Seekers Mentored By An Eccentric Tycoon A Practical, Step-By-Step Dawn Routine To Protect Early Hours Neuroscience-Backed Practices For Focus, Creativity, And Energy Strategies To Shield Mornings From Digital Distractions Practical Exercises And Prompts For Exercise, Renewal, And Growth After Finishing The 5 Am Club – Own Your Morning, Readers Gain A Repeatable Framework For Starting Each Day With Purpose, Calm, And Momentum. It Leaves You Feeling Empowered To Think Bigger, Act Smarter, And Live With Intention, Long After The Last Page.
works.authorDescription: Robin Sharma is a Canadian writer, best known for his The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari book series. Sharma worked as a litigation lawyer until age 25, when he self-published MegaLiving (1994), a book on stress management and spirituality. He initially also self-published The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari, which was then picked up for wider distribution by HarperCollins. Sharma has published 12 other books, and founded the training company Sharma Leadership International.

works.description: A non-fiction narrative about the build-up of the 2000s housing bubble and the eccentric investors who bet against the market.

works.title: Silent Spring
works.author: Rachel Carson
works.description: Discover A Remarkable Journey Of Courage And Resilience With This Inspiring Tale. Follow The Story Of Manjari Jaruhar, Who Defied Expectations And Overcame Significant Challenges To Become The First Woman From Bihar To Join The Elite Police Cadre Of India. This Powerful Narrative Showcases Her Grit And Determination As She Navigates A Male-Dominated Field While Breaking Stereotypes And Proving Herself. Set Against The Backdrop Of Pivotal Events Like The Bhagalpur Blindings And The 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots, This Book Offers A Unique Insight Into The Indian Police Service From A Woman's Perspective. Each Chapter Unravels The Complexities Of Her Experiences, Portraying Her Struggle And Triumphs Within A System Often Resistant To Change. Madam Sir Is More Than Just A Memoir; It's A Masterclass In Leadership And An Uplifting Reminder That With Perseverance, Anyone Can Reach For Their Dreams. Whether You're Looking For Motivation Or Simply Seeking A Captivating Read, This Story Will Resonate Deeply And Inspire You To Pursue Your Dreams With Vigor. Immerse Yourself In An Extraordinary Account That Redefines What It Means To Be A Leader. Let Manjari's Journey Inspire You To Challenge The Odds And Reach For The Impossible Heights You Aspire To Attain.
works.authorDescription:
Rachel Louise Carson (May 27, 1907 – April 14, 1964) was an American marine biologist, writer, and conservationist whose sea trilogy (1941–1955) and book Silent Spring (1962) are credited with advancing marine conservation and the global environmental movement.
Carson began her career as an aquatic biologist in the U.S. Bureau of Fisheries, and became a full-time nature writer in the 1950s. Her widely praised 1951 bestseller The Sea Around Us won her a U.S. National Book Award, recognition as a gifted writer, and financial security. Its success prompted the republication of her first book, Under the Sea Wind (1941), in 1952, which was followed by The Edge of the Sea in 1955 — both were also bestsellers. This sea trilogy explores the whole of ocean life from the shores to the depths.
Late in the 1950s, Carson turned her attention to conservation, especially some problems she believed were caused by synthetic pesticides. The result was the book Silent Spring (1962), which brought environ...

works.title: Daring Greatly
works.author: Brene Brown
works.description: Your Ultimate Guide To Exploring Goa Goa, With Its Stunning Golden Beaches, Charming Fishing Villages, And Rich Cultural Heritage, Is A Treasure Waiting To Be Discovered. With Dk Eyewitness Top 10 Goa , You'll Effortlessly Navigate Through This Vibrant Destination, Ensuring You Experience All The Highlights That Make Goa Unforgettable. What Awaits You This Updated 2023 Travel Guide Is Packed With Essential Information That Will Make Your Trip Planning As Smooth As A Gentle Sea Breeze. Inside, You'll Find: Up-To-Date Insider Tips That Ensure Your Safety And Enhance Your Experience. Top 10 Must-See Spots In Goa, Including Stunning Locations Like Basilica De Bom Jesus And Old Goa. Insight Into Goa's Most Interesting Areas, Highlighting The Best Choices For Sightseeing, Exquisite Food, And Local Shopping. Themed Lists That Uncover Secret Beaches, Thrilling Outdoor Activities, Unique Shops, And Culinary Delights. Easy-To-Follow Itineraries For A Day, A Weekend Getaway, Or Your Entire Week In Goa. A Laminated Pull-Out Map And Four Full-Color Area Maps To Help Guide Your Adventures. Compact And Convenient This Guide Is Designed For Travelers Who Are Always On The Go.
