works.title: The Happiness Hypothesis
works.author: Jonathan Haidt
works.description: The Happiness Hypothesis: Finding Modern Truth in Ancient Wisdom is a 2006 book written by American social psychologist Jonathan Haidt.
works.authorDescription:
Jonathan David Haidt ( HYTE; born October 19, 1963) is an American social psychologist and author. He is a professor of business and  society and the Thomas Cooley Chair of Ethical Leadership at the New York University Stern School of Business. Haidt's main areas of study are the psychology of morality and moral emotions.
Haidt's main contributions to the field of psychology come from his theory of moral foundations, which attempts to explain the origins of human moral reasoning on the basis of innate "modules", resulting from biological and cultural evolution. The theory was later further developed to explain varitation in moral reasoning as it relates to political ideology, positing that people arrive at different political orientations due to prioritizing different sets of morals. Haidt's current research applies moral psychology to business ethics.
Haidt has written multiple popular psychology books, including The Happiness Hypothesis (2006) examining the relationship between ancie...

works.title: Swang
works.author: Gyan Chaturvedi
works.description: A biting Hindi satirical novel highlighting the absurdities, corruption, and hypocrisies of the modern medical and political systems in India.
works.authorDescription: Gyan Chaturvedi is an Indian writer and satirist in Hindi literature, awarded the Padma Shri for his contributions.

works.title: The Sixth Extinction
works.author: Elizabeth Kolbert
works.description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning book arguing that the Earth is currently amid a modern, man-made mass extinction event.
works.authorDescription: Elizabeth Kolbert is an American journalist, author, and visiting fellow at Williams College, known for her environmental writing.

works.title: Business Adventures
works.author: John Brooks
works.description: A collection of insightful, narrative-driven case studies about iconic Wall Street moments and corporate disasters.
works.authorDescription: John Brooks was an American writer and long-time contributor to The New Yorker, specializing in financial journalism.

works.title: Desperately Seeking Shah Rukh
works.author: Shrayana Bhattacharya
works.description: This Is A Memoir-Style Narrative That Blends Personal Storytelling With Cultural Observations. Its Central Themes Center On Chasing Dreams, Discovering Identity, And Finding Belonging Within The Vibrant World Of Cinema And City Life. The Ideal Reader Is Adults Who Enjoy Intimate, Reflective Nonfiction, Cultural Travel Narratives, And Bollywood-Inspired Storytelling. The Tone Is Candid, Witty, And Hopeful, Inviting Readers To See Their Own Experiences Reflected In A Cosmopolitan Journey. The Reading Experience Unfolds Through Vivid, Story-Led Chapters And Crisp, Cinematic Prose. It Blends Intimate Anecdotes With Sensory Detail—Soundtracks, Street Flavors, And The Energy Of Bustling Streets—To Create A Warm, Immersive Atmosphere. What Makes The Experience Distinctive Is The Author’S Voice: Personable, Sharp, And Unafraid To Laugh At Missteps While Celebrating Moments Of Courage And Clarity. Readers Move Through A Series Of Snapshots That Feel Both Universal And Deeply Personal, Encouraging Reflection Without Feeling Weighty. Story-Led Memoir With A Focus On Ambition, Identity, And Emotional Resilience Accessible, Engaging Writing That Captures Mood, Setting, And Character With Vivid Detail Thoughtful Cultural Observations And Moments Of Humor That Illuminate Cross-Cultural Experiences A Voyage Through Personal Growth That Invites Empathy, Curiosity, And Reflection Reading This Book Leaves You With A Renewed Sense Of Possibility: A Deeper Understanding Of How Culture Shapes Us, A Curiosity To Explore New Perspectives, And The Motivation To Pursue Your Own Dreams With Renewed Confidence And Joy.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Quiet
works.author: Susan Cain
works.description: A cultural critique exploring the power of introverts in a world that can't stop talking, challenging the 'Extrovert Ideal'.
works.authorDescription: Susan Cain is an American writer and lecturer whose work focuses on introversion and the psychological impact of modern culture.

works.title: The Power of Myth
works.author: Joseph Campbell
works.description: NATIONAL BESTSELLER • An extraordinary book that reveals how the themes and symbols of ancient narratives continue to bring meaning to birth, death, love, and war. The Power of Myth launched an extraordinary resurgence of interest in Joseph Campbell and his work. A preeminent scholar, writer, and teacher, he has had a profound influence on millions of people—including Star Wars creator George Lucas. To Campbell, mythology was the “song of the universe, the music of the spheres.” With Bill Moyers, one of America’s most prominent journalists, as his thoughtful and engaging interviewer, The Power of Myth touches on subjects from modern marriage to virgin births, from Jesus to John Lennon, offering a brilliant combination of intelligence and wit. From stories of the gods and goddesses of ancient Greece and Rome to traditions of Buddhism, Hinduism and Christianity, a broad array of themes are considered that together identify the universality of human experience across time and culture. An impeccable match of interviewer and subject, a timeless distillation of Campbell’s work, The Power of Myth continues to exert a profound influence on our culture.

works.title: The Kite Runner
works.author: Khaled Hosseini
works.description: The Kite Runner - Invites You Into 1975 Afghanistan Where Twelve-Year-Old Amir Dreams Of Winning The Local Kite-Fighting Tournament With The Steady Help Of His Friend Hassan. A Tale Of Friendship, Loyalty, And The Quest For Redemption, It Speaks To Readers Who Enjoy Thoughtful Literary Fiction And Coming-Of-Age Journeys, With An Emotional Tone That Is Poignant, Hopeful, And Introspective. The Narrative, As The Kite Runner Unfolds, Follows Amir's Childhood World, The Changing Country, And The Moment That Changes Everything. It Traces His Family's Escape To America After The Russian Invasion And His Eventual Return To Taliban-Ruled Afghanistan To Seek Forgiveness. The Result Is A Richly Drawn, Deeply Human Story About How Loyalty, Guilt, And Love Shape A Life. Written With Clear, Evocative Prose, This Novel Blends Intimate Memory With Sweeping Historical Drama. The Book's Structure Lets The Emotional Heartbeat Drive The Pace, Pairing Tense, High-Stakes Moments With Quiet Reflection. Its Vivid Setting And Cultural Detail Make The Journey Feel Personal And Universal. Core Story Elements: 1975 Kabul, Kite-Fighting Tournament, Amir And Hassan, A Life-Changing Event, Exile To America, And A Return To A War-Torn Homeland Standout Features: Richly Drawn Characters, Emotional Depth, And A Powerful Exploration Of Loyalty And Redemption Reading Experience: Emotionally Resonant, Character-Driven Narrative With Historical Context Writing Style: Clear, Compassionate Prose That Captures Atmosphere And Heart After Finishing The Kite Runner, Readers Gain A Deeper Understanding Of Forgiveness, Courage, And The Enduring Power Of Confronting The Past. This Story Stays With You Long After The Last Page, Inviting Reflection On Friendship, Memory, And The Possibility Of Redemption.
works.authorDescription: Khaled Hosseini or Khalid Husseini is an Afghan and American novelist, UNHCR goodwill ambassador, and former physician. His debut novel The Kite Runner (2003) was a critical and commercial success; the book and his subsequent novels have all been at least partially set in Afghanistan and have featured an Afghan as the protagonist. Hosseini's novels have spread awareness about Afghanistan's people and culture.

works.title: Educated
works.author: Tara Westover
works.description: A powerful memoir about a woman who grows up in a survivalist family in rural Idaho and eventually earns a PhD from Cambridge.
works.authorDescription: Tara Westover is an American memoirist, essayist, and historian.

works.title: Read Write Own
works.author: Chris Dixon
works.description: A compelling case for how blockchain technology can take the internet back from corporate monopolies and usher in a decentralized 'Web3' era.
works.authorDescription: Chris Dixon is an American internet entrepreneur and venture capitalist at Andreessen Horowitz.

works.title: Seeking Wisdom
works.author: Peter Bevelin
works.description: A distillation of Charles Munger's multidisciplinary mental models for rational thinking and avoiding cognitive biases.
works.authorDescription: Peter Bevelin is a Swedish investor and author who extensively researches human behavior and the wisdom of Buffett and Munger.

works.title: The Spy Chronicles: RAW, ISI and the Illusion of Peace
works.author: A.S. Dulat & Asad Durrani
works.description: A candid, unprecedented dialogue between the former chiefs of India's RAW and Pakistan's ISI discussing geopolitics and intelligence.
works.authorDescription: A.S. Dulat is a former chief of India's RAW. Asad Durrani is a former head of Pakistan's ISI.

works.title: Black Tornado
works.author: Sandeep Unnithan
works.description: A fast-paced, minute-by-minute narrative of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks and the Indian military response.
works.authorDescription: Sandeep Unnithan is an Indian journalist, author, and military affairs expert.

works.title: Godaan
works.author: Munshi Premchand
works.description: Godan (Hindi) - Is A Sweeping, Humane Novel That Follows Hori, A Farmer, And His Family As They Confront Debt, Exploitation, And The Pressures Of A Nation In Transition. A Cornerstone Of Hindi Literature And Social Realism, Godan Examines Caste, Capitalism, And The Everyday Courage Of Ordinary People. It Is Ideal For Readers Of Hindi Fiction, Students Of Indian History, And Anyone Who Values Character-Driven Stories With Social Depth. The Tone Is Thoughtful, Serious, And Deeply Humane. Premchand's Godan Is Written In Lucid, Accessible Prose And Structured Around Two Interwoven Narratives—The Rhythms Of Village Life And The Pull Of Urban Centers—Creating A Balanced, Lifelike Portrait Of A Society On The Edge Of Change. The Story Centers On Hori And His Family—Dhaniya, Roopa, Sona, Gobar, Jhuniya—Whose Experiences Illuminate Larger Forces At Work: The Power Of Moneylenders, The Weight Of Caste, And The Shifting Economy That Erodes Old Feudal Loyalties While Birthing New Forms Of Labor And Industry. The Novel's Pacing, Vivid Scenes, And Plainspoken Voice Invite Readers To Walk With These Characters Through Triumphs And Trials Without Sensationalism, Making Hardship Feel Real And Relatable. With Its Epic Scope And Intimate Detail, Godan Offers A Nuanced Window Into Rural Life And The Social Fabric Of Early 20Th‑Century India. The Intertwined Narratives Encourage Readers To See How Private Struggles Reflect Public Change, And How Individuals Navigate Tradition As Economic Forces Reshape Society. The Book Blends Family Drama With Social Critique, Painting A Convincing Panorama Of A Country In Flux And Inviting Reflection That Remains Relevant Today. Two Interwoven Narratives Blending Village Life With Urban Context Memorable Characters: Hori And His Family—Dhaniya, Roopa, Sona, Gobar, Jhuniya Exploration Of Caste, Moneylending, And The Shift From Feudalism To Capitalism Vivid, Accessible Hindi Prose That Captures Rural India And Its Rhythms Historical And Social Insights That Deepen Understanding Of India's Past Thoughtful, Humane Storytelling With Lasting Emotional Impact After Finishing Godan, Readers Gain A Deeper Empathy For Indian Farmers, A Clearer Understanding Of India's Transitional Era, And A Lasting Appreciation For Premchand's Humane Storytelling That Lingers Long After The Last Page.
works.authorDescription: Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, better known as Munshi Premchand based on his pen name Premchand, was an Indian writer famous for his modern Hindustani literature.

works.title: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!
works.author: Richard Feynman
works.description: Winner Of The Nobel Prize For Physics In 1965, Richard Feynman Was One Of The World's Greatest Theoretical Physicists, But He Was Also A Man Who Fell, Often Jumped, Into Adventure. An Artist, Safecracker, Practical Joker And Storyteller, Feynman's Life Was A Series Of Combustible Combinations Made Possible By His Unique Mixture Of High Intelligence, Unquenchable Curiosity And Eternal Scepticism. Over A Period Of Years, Feynman's Conversations With His Friend Ralph Leighton Were First Taped And Then Set Down As They Appear Here, Little Changed From Their Spoken Form, Giving A Wise, Funny, Passionate And Totally Honest Self-Portrait Of One Of The Greatest Men Of Our Age.
works.authorDescription:
Richard Phillips Feynman was an American theoretical physicist. He shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics with Julian Schwinger and Shin'ichirō Tomonaga "for their fundamental work in quantum electrodynamics (QED), with deep-ploughing consequences for the physics of elementary particles".
He is also known for his work in the path integral formulation of quantum mechanics, the theory of the physics of the superfluidity of supercooled liquid helium, and the parton model. Feynman developed a pictorial representation scheme for the mathematical expressions describing the behavior of subatomic particles, which later became known as Feynman diagrams and remains widely used.

works.title: The Grid
works.author: Gretchen Bakke
works.description: An exploration of the fragile American electrical grid, its history, and its urgent need for modernization in the renewable era.
works.authorDescription: Gretchen Bakke is a cultural anthropologist and writer whose work focuses on energy infrastructure and society.

works.title: Nudge
works.author: Thaler & Sunstein
works.description: A behavioral economics book on 'choice architecture', showing how minor tweaks can gently push people toward better decisions.
works.authorDescription: Richard Thaler is a Nobel-winning economist. Cass Sunstein is a legal scholar. Both are American academics.

works.title: Dusra Lucknow
works.author: Nadeem Hasnain
works.description: An ethnographic and cultural exploration mapping the hidden, pluralistic, and subaltern history of the city of Lucknow.
works.authorDescription: Nadeem Hasnain is an Indian social anthropologist and author specializing in the sociology of Muslims and Indian culture.

works.title: Remarkably Bright Creatures
works.author: Shelby Van Pelt
works.description: Remarkably Bright Creatures Is A Tender, Character-Driven Contemporary Novel About Grief, Memory, And An Extraordinary Friendship. Set At Sowell Bay Aquarium, It Follows Tova Sullivan, A Night-Shift Cleaner Who Is Learning To Live With Loss, And Marcellus, A Giant Pacific Octopus Who Notices Everything But Speaks Through Quiet Acts Of Care. Written For Adults Who Crave Moving, Hopeful Stories, This Book Carries A Warm, Hopeful Tone That Feels Both Intimate And Luminous. In Remarkably Bright Creatures , The Narration Blends Tova's Grounded, Practical Perspective With Marcellus's Patient, Observant Presence, Delivering A Gentle Mystery Told In Short, Thoughtful Chapters. The Book Is Written To Be Accessible And Moving, With The Sowell Bay Aquarium Providing A Vivid Backdrop And A Rhythm That Balances Quiet Daily Life With Moments Of Wonder. The Experience Is Rich With Humor, Warmth, And Memorable Creatures Who Help Illuminate Grief And Resilience, Inviting Readers To Lean Into Tenderness And Curiosity As The Story Reveals Its Truths At A Natural Pace. Key Content Elements: Grief, Friendship, A Decades-Old Mystery, Sowell Bay Aquarium, Strong Bond Between A Cleaner And An Octopus Interactive Or Standout Features: Warm Dialogue, Gentle Humor, Memorable Sea-Life Cast Learning Outcomes Or Experiences: Empathy, Resilience, The Healing Power Of Listening And Connection Writing Or Illustration Style: Lyrical, Accessible Prose With Vivid Setting And A Calm, Hopeful Rhythm What Awaits After Finishing Remarkably Bright Creatures Is A Lingering Sense Of Hope And A Renewed Belief In The Power Of Listening And Unlikely Friendship. It Stays With You, Reminding You That The Past Can Shed Light On A Future That Once Seemed Impossible.
works.authorDescription: Shelby Van Pelt is an American writer. Her debut novel Remarkably Bright Creatures (2022) has sold over 4 million copies and was adapted into a 2026 film. She grew up in Tacoma, Washington, graduated from Claremont McKenna College in 2002, and spent the next several years working as a financial consultant on litigation. After graduation, Van Pelt spent several years living in Atlanta, where she began writing Remarkably Bright Creatures in 2013. The novel was primarily written in 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic.

works.title: My Experiments with Truth
works.author: M.K. Gandhi
works.description: The Story Of My Experiments With Truth Is Gandhi’S Intimate Autobiography, Tracing A Life Shaped By Nonviolence, Truth, And Service. Written For Readers Curious About History, Philosophy, And How A Steadfast Conscience Can Spark Social Change, This Spare, Honest Memoir Invites All Ages To Explore The Roots Of Satyagraha And Ahimsa With Warmth And Insight. Structured As A Chronological Journey, The Story Of My Experiments With Truth Reveals Gandhi’S Early Years, Family Life, Schooling In India And London, His Experiments With Diet And Vegetarianism, And His Awakening In South Africa Amid Racial Prejudice. Through Plain, Reflective Prose, It Explains How Each Experience Fed A Growing Commitment To Truth And Nonviolence, And How Those Ideas Informed His Leadership In India's Freedom Movement. Readers Are Invited To See Not Just The Milestones But The Questions Gandhi Wrestled With—How To Balance Personal Faith With Public Responsibility, How To Endure Hardship, And How Ordinary Choices Can Become Radical Acts Of Courage. The Story Of My Experiments With Truth Offers Both Historical Insight And Timeless Guidance For Anyone Seeking Integrity In A Complex World. Autobiographical Journey From Childhood To 1921 Core Themes Of Truth, Nonviolence, And Simple Living Key Episodes: Education, London, Dietetic Experiments, South Africa, And The Rise Of India's Independence Movement Plainspoken, Reflective Writing With Philosophical Insights Timeless Guidance On Integrity, Courage, And Social Change Readers Finish With A Clearer Sense Of How Truth, Courage, And Nonviolent Action Can Transform Daily Life And Society. The Story Of My Experiments With Truth Invites Reflection, Resilience, And A Renewed Commitment To Living With Purpose—Long After The Last Page Is Turned.
works.authorDescription:
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi ( GA(H)N-dee; 2 October 1869 – 30 January 1948) was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who employed nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule, and to later inspire movements for civil rights and freedom across the world. The honorific Mahātmā (Sanskrit: "great-souled", "venerable"), first applied to him in 1914 in South Africa, is now used throughout the world.
Born and raised in a Hindu family in coastal Gujarat, Gandhi was trained in the law at the Inner Temple in London and was called to the bar at the age of 22. After two uncertain years in India, where he was unable to start a successful law practice, Gandhi moved to South Africa in 1893 to represent an Indian merchant in a lawsuit. He went on to live in South Africa for the next 21 years. Here, Gandhi raised a family and first employed nonviolent resistance in a campaign for civil rights. In 1915, aged 45, he returne...

works.title: The Spy, The Archer & Brida
works.author: Paulo Coelho
works.description: The Archer Tells The Story Of Tetsuya, A Master Archer Who Has Retreated From The Spotlight, And The Curious Boy Who Seeks His Guidance. Through Spare, Contemplative Prose, Paulo Coelho Invites Readers Into A Gentle Fable About Living With Courage, Intention, And Meaning. Written For Adults And Thoughtful Readers Who Crave Reflection, The Archer Offers An Inspiring, Comforting Voice That Makes Complex Questions Feel Approachable. Structured As Intimate Conversations And Parables, The Archer Unfolds In Clear, Accessible Steps—Short Chapters, Quiet Dialogue, And Practical Reflections That Reward Slow Reading. Tetsuya Shares Experiences From A Life Devoted To Mastery, While The Boy's Questions Spark Insights About Courage, Risk, Connecting Action To The Soul, And Pursuing Passion With Purpose. The Experience Is Meditative And Uplifting, Inviting Readers To Pause, Notice, And Apply Each Lesson Without Feeling Overwhelmed. Whether You Read For Personal Growth Or To Savor Coelho's Graceful Storytelling, The Archer Blends Storytelling With Wisdom, Offering A Reliable Framework For Living Well. The Book's Calm Pace And Lucid Language Make The Concepts Approachable—Learning Feels Like A Personal Conversation Rather Than A Lesson Plan, And The Ideas Stay With You Long After You Turn The Last Page. The Archer's Thoughtful Approach Invites Readers To See Challenges As Invitations To Grow And To Explore How Small, Deliberate Steps Can Shape A Meaningful Life. Courage, Risk-Taking, And Pursuing Purpose Connection Between Action And Soul, And Making A Difference Short, Dialogue-Driven Chapters With Timeless Wisdom Accessible, Graceful, Contemplative Writing Perfect For Solo Reading Or Thoughtful Discussion Groups After Finishing The Archer, Readers Often Feel Steadier, More Willing To Take Bold Steps, And Inspired To Live With Intention. It Invites You To View The Journey As The Reward, Leaving You With A Calmer Confidence And A Deeper Sense Of What Truly Matters.
works.authorDescription: Paulo Coelho de Souza ( KWEL-yoo, koo-EL-yoo, -⁠yoh, Portuguese: [ˈpawlu kuˈeʎu]; born 24 August 1947) is a Brazilian lyricist and novelist. He has been a member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters since 2002. His 1988 novel The Alchemist is an international best-seller.

works.title: Relentless: A Memoir
works.author: Yashwant Sinha
works.description: Relentless Traces Yashwant Sinha’S Extraordinary Journey From Modest Beginnings In Bihar To The Highest Corridors Of Power In India. Part Memoir And Part Political History, This Engaging Book Is Perfect For Readers Who Enjoy Intimate Portraits Of Public Life And The Forces That Shape A Nation. Aimed At Adults With An Interest In Politics, Governance, And Leadership, The Tone Is Candid, Inspirational, And Thoughtful—An Adventure Through Public Service, Sacrifice, And Steadfast Determination. Written In Sinha’S Own Voice, Relentless Moves Across Decades And Continents—From Bureaucrats Bicycling To Work In Small-Town Bihar To The Autobahn Of Bonn; From The Benches Of The Indian Parliament To The Podium Of The United Nations General Assembly. Having Worked With Three Prime Ministers And Two Chief Ministers And Serving As External Affairs Minister And Twice As Finance Minister, The Book Offers A Frontline View Of India’S Transformation—From A Fledgling Postcolonial Democracy To A Rising Economic Powerhouse. It Blends Personal Stories With Candid Commentary On Politics, Religion, Democracy And Its Institutions, As Well As Family, Sacrifice, And The Relentless Pursuit Of Bigger Dreams. The Narrative Balances Memoir With Accessible Analysis, Presenting Key Moments In Leadership, Policy, And Institutional Life Without Shying Away From Hard Choices. It Invites Readers To See The Human Side Of Governance—The Late-Night Conversations, The Compromises, The Costs—And To Understand How Ideas About Democracy And Development Take Shape In The Real World. If You’Re Curious About The People, Events, And Ideas That Have Charted India’S Modern Course, Relentless Offers A Clear, Engaging Path Through It All. Biographical Milestones From Bureaucracy To Ministerial Roles And Parliamentarian Work Inside Perspectives On India's Political Landscape, Including Leaders And Major Parties Behind-The-Scenes Look At Governance, Policy Decisions, And The Nation's Economic Rise Personal Stories Of Family, Sacrifice, Resilience, And Relentless Ambition Accessible, Narrative Writing That Blends Memoir With Thoughtful Political Commentary Relentless Leaves Readers With A Deeper Appreciation Of Public Life And A Nuanced View Of India’S Ongoing Evolution. After Finishing The Book, You’Ll Gain Insight Into Leadership, Democracy, And The Personal Cost And Reward Of Serving A Nation—Plus A Sense Of Hope And Responsibility For What Comes Next.
works.authorDescription: Yashwant Sinha (Hindustani pronunciation: [jəʃˈʋən̪t̪ sɪnˈɦɑː], born 6 November 1937) is an Indian politician and retired Indian Administrative Service officer. He served as the Minister of Finance from 1990 until 1991 under Prime Minister Chandra Shekhar and again from March 1998 to July 2002 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He also served as the Minister of External Affairs from July 2002 until May 2004. He was a senior leader of the BJP before he left the party on 21 April 2018. In 2022, he was the Presidential candidate of India for the opposition.

works.title: Tamas
works.author: Bhisham Sahni
works.description: Tamas (Hindi) - Is A Hindi-Language Edition Crafted For Readers Who Love Immersive, Thoughtful Storytelling. This Portable Is Ideal For Adults And Hindi-Language Enthusiasts Seeking A Calm, Engaging Reading Experience—Perfect For Curling Up At Home, Commuting, Or Gifting Someone Special. The Book Is Written In Clear, Flowing Prose, Organized Into Accessible Chapters That Make The Journey Feel Gentle And Rewarding. The Experience Is Enjoyable Because The Pacing Respects The Reader's Time While Inviting Reflection. Tamas (Hindi) - Presents Its Content Through Intimate Storytelling, With A Thoughtful Rhythm And A Focus On Readability That Makes The Journey Feel Fulfilling. The Language Flows In Hindi, Offering Readers A Natural Reading Experience That Helps Deepen Familiarity With Rhythm And Expression. The Portable Format Keeps You Close To The Narrative, Making It Easy To Pick Up, Pause, And Return—Whether You’Re Curling Up With A Blanket At Home Or Taking A Quick Break During The Day. Portable Edition For Reading On The Go Clear, Flowing Hindi Prose Designed For Comfortable Reading Engaging Storytelling With A Steady Pace That Invites Reflection Great Gift For Hindi Readers And Learners Supports Hindi Language Practice And Vocabulary Growth After Finishing Tamas (Hindi) - , Readers Carry A Sense Of Connection And Calm, Along With A Renewed Curiosity About Everyday Moments. This Edition Offers Warmth And Lasting Value, Inviting You To Revisit Its Pages And Carry The Experience With You Into Daily Life.
works.authorDescription: Bhisham Sahni (8 August 1915 – 11 July 2003) was an Indian writer, playwright in Hindi and an actor, most famous for his novel Tamas ("Darkness"/'Ignorance") and the television screenplay adaptation of the same name, a powerful and passionate account of the partition of India. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan for literature in 1998, and Sahitya Akademi Fellowship in 2002. He was the younger brother of the noted Hindi film actor, Balraj Sahni.

works.title: Kaghazi Hai Pairahan
works.author: Ismat Chughtai
works.description: The fiercely honest and uninhibited memoir of one of Urdu literature's most revolutionary and controversial female voices.
works.authorDescription: Ismat Chughtai was an Indian Urdu novelist, short story writer, and filmmaker known for her progressive, feminist literature.

works.title: Shuddhipatra, Khela
works.author: Neelakshi Singh
works.description: समाजातील ज्या घटकांवर पिढ्यान् पिढ्या अन्याय झाला, त्या घटकांना न्याय्य वागणूक मिळावी, म्हणून भारतीय संविधानाने अनुसूचित जाती- जमाती अत्याचार प्रतिबंधक कायदा पारित केला. अल्पसंख्यांक समाजाच्या रक्षणासाठीही विशेषत्वाने कायदे करण्यात आले. त्यामुळे त्या त्या समाज घटकांचे अवमानकारक उल्लेख कायद्याच्या कचाट्यात आपसूकच आले. पण शब्दकोशासारख्या भाषिक वैभवामध्ये जातिवाचक उल्लेख अर्थासह दिल्याने कोणाचा अपमान होऊ शकतो? भावना दुखावतात? भाषांवर निरतिशय प्रेम असलेल्या एका तज्ज्ञाने शब्दकोशातील ते सहा शब्द वगळले जाऊ नयेत, म्हणून दिलेल्या कायदेशीर लढ्याचे चित्रण करणारी ही सामाजिक कादंबरी आहे. लेखकाविषयी : मराठीतील अव्वल दर्जाचे कथाकार व कादंबरीकार म्हणून परिचित. प्रवासवर्णन, स्फुटलेखन, नाटक, इत्यादी साहित्यप्रकारांतही लेखन. अनेक लघुकथा व दीर्घकथांचे लेखन. त्यांच्या अनेक कादंबऱ्यांचे भारतीय भाषांमध्ये अनुवाद. १९८८ ते १९९२ या कालावधीत अखिल भारतीय मराठी साहित्प महामंडळाचे अध्यक्ष आणि १९९५ ते २००६ या कालावधीत महाराष्ट्र साहित्य परिषद, पुणे या संस्थेचे अध्यक्षपदगंगार्पण, कृष्णजन्म, लांडगा या कथासंग्रहांना राज्यशासनाने सर्वोत्कृष्ट कथासंग्रह पुरस्कार तर अखेरचे आत्मचरित्र या कादंबरीला राज्यशासनाचा सर्वोत्कृष्ट कादंबरी पुरस्कार. याखेरीज, ना.सी. फडके पुरस्कार, ह.ना. आपटे पुरस्कार, शंकर पाटील पारितोषिक, आनंदीबाई शिर्के पारितोषिक, श्री. दा. पानवलकर पुरस्कार अशा अनेक साहित्यविषयक पुरस्कारांचे मानकरी. महाराष्ट्र राज्य गुजराथी अकादमीतर्फे उत्कृष्ट साहित्य निर्मितीसाठी देण्यात येणारा वर्ष २०२२- २३ साठीचा कवी नर्मद मराठी साहित्प पुरस्कार प्राप्त
works.authorDescription: Neelakshi Singh (born 17 March 1978) is an Indian novelist and short story writer in Hindi language. She won Sahitya Akademi Golden Jubilee Young Writers Award, Kalinga Book of the year award 2021 and Valley of Words Award 2022.

works.title: Jitni Mitti Utna Sona & Lapujhanna
works.author: Ashok Pande
works.description: कुमाऊँ, उत्तराखंड के सुदूर हिमालयी इलाक़े में भारत-तिब्बत सीमा से लगी व्यांस, दारमा और चौंदास घाटियों में निवास करने वाले लोग सदियों से तिब्बत के साथ व्यापार करते आए हैं। अपने आप को रं कहने वाले ये जन अद्वितीय सांस्कृतिक और सामाजिक परंपराओं से लैस एक अनूठी सभ्यता के ध्वजवाहक हैं। यह यात्रावृत्त इन्हीं घाटियों में की गई अनेक लंबी शोध-यात्राओं का परिणाम है। यह आपका परिचय संसार के एक ऐसे रहस्यमय हिस्से से करवाएगा जिसके बारे में बहुत कम प्रामाणिक कार्य हुआ है।इस किताब में आपको बेहद मुश्किल परिस्थितियों में हिमालय की गोद में निवास करने वाले रं समाज की सांस्कृतिक संपन्नता के दर्शन तो होंगे ही, आप उस अजेय जिजीविषा और अतिमानवीय साहस से भी रू-ब-रू होंगे जिसके बिना इन दुर्गम घाटियों में जीने की कल्पना तक नहीं की जा सकती।मानवशास्त्रीय महत्त्व के विवरणों से भरपूर इस यात्रावृत्त में कथा, गल्प, कविता, लोक साहित्य, और स्मृति के ताने-बाने से एक तिलिस्म रचा गया है जिसमें बुज़ुर्गों के सुनाए क़िस्सों की परिचित ऊष्मा भी है और अजनाने भूगोल में यात्रा करने का रोमांच भी।
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Akaal mein Utsav
works.author: Pankaj Subeer
works.description: A compelling piece of Hindi literature exploring the resilience and human spirit amidst crisis and famine.
works.authorDescription: Pankaj Subeer is an acclaimed Indian Hindi author and poet known for his nuanced storytelling.

works.title: The Forgotten Highlander
works.author: Alistair Urquhart
works.description: Alistair Urquhart was a soldier in the Gordon Highlanders captured by the Japanese in Singapore. He not only survived working on the notorious Bridge on the River Kwai , but he was subsequently taken on one of the Japanese 'hellships' which was torpedoed. Nearly everyone else on board died and Urquhart spent 5 days alone on a raft in the South China Sea before being rescued by a whaling ship. He was taken to Japan and then forced to work in a mine near Nagasaki. Two months later a nuclear bomb dropped just ten miles away . . . This is the extraordinary story of a young men, conscripted at nineteen and whose father was a Somme Veteran, survived not just one, but three close encounters with death - encounters which killed nearly all his comrades.

works.title: Founders at Work
works.author: Jessica Livingston
works.description: Founders at Work: Stories of Startups' Early Days is a collection of interviews with founders of famous technology companies about what happened in the very earliest days. These people are celebrities now. What was it like when they were just a couple friends with an idea? Founders like Steve Wozniak (Apple), Caterina Fake (Flickr), Mitch Kapor (Lotus), Max Levchin (PayPal), and Sabeer Bhatia (Hotmail) tell you in their own words about their surprising and often very funny discoveries as they learned how to build a company. Where did they get the ideas that made them rich? How did they convince investors to back them? What went wrong, and how did they recover? Nearly all technical people have thought of one day starting or working for a startup. For them, this book is the closest you can come to being a fly on the wall at a successful startup, to learn how it's done. But ultimately these interviews are required reading for anyone who wants to understand business, because startups are business reduced to its essence. The reason their founders become rich is that startups do what businesses do—create value—more intensively than almost any other part of the economy. How? What are the secrets that make successful startups so insanely productive? Read this book, and let the founders themselves tell you.

works.title: Emotional Intelligence
works.author: Daniel Goleman
works.description: From the Trade Paperback edition.

works.title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
works.author: Rebecca Skloot
works.description: A heartbreaking account of a medical miracle: how one woman’s cells – taken without her knowledge – have saved countless lives. The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks is a true story of race, class, injustice and exploitation. ‘No dead woman has done more for the living . . . A fascinating, harrowing, necessary book.’ – Hilary Mantel, Guardian With an introduction Sarah Moss, author of by author of Summerwater. Her name was Henrietta Lacks, but scientists know her as HeLa. Born a poor black tobacco farmer, her cancer cells – taken without asking her – became a multimillion-dollar industry and one of the most important tools in medicine. Yet Henrietta’s family did not learn of her ‘immortality’ until more than twenty years after her death, with devastating consequences . . . Rebecca Skloot’s moving account is the story of the life, and afterlife, of one woman who changed the medical world forever. Balancing the beauty and drama of scientific discovery with dark questions about who owns the stuff our bodies are made of, The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks is an extraordinary journey in search of the soul and story of a real woman, whose cells live on today in all four corners of the world. Now an HBO film starring Oprah Winfrey and Rose Byrne.

works.title: Rocket Boys
works.author: Homer Hickam
works.description: An autobiographical coming-of-age story about a teenager in a coal-mining town who builds rockets and eventually joins NASA.
works.authorDescription: Homer Hickam is an American author, Vietnam War veteran, and former NASA engineer.

works.title: Shoe Dog
works.author: Phil Knight
works.description: Shoe Dog Is The Candid Memoir Of Phil Knight, The Founder Of Nike, Tracing His Leap From Borrowing $50 To Building A Global Athletic Empire. This Is A Gripping Business Memoir That Will Resonate With Aspiring Entrepreneurs, Sports Fans, And Readers Who Value Bold, True Stories. The Tone Is Honest, Adventurous, And Uplifting, Inviting You To Understand Why One Visionary Made A Mission Out Of Turning Ideas Into Motion. Written In Knight’S Own Voice, This Memoir Unfolds As A Chronological Tapestry Of Early Risks, Long Nights, And Unlikely Partnerships. The Book Reads Like A Behind-The-Scenes Diary, Weaving Humor And Humility With Hard-Won Lessons About Bootstrapping, Leadership, And Brand-Building. The Narrative Captures The Daily Grind—The Negotiations, The Sleepless Deadlines, And The Stubborn Faith That Momentum Can Be Built One Careful Step At A Time. In Shoe Dog, Knight Shares Crossroad Moments, Sacrifices, And Turning Points That Transformed A Scrappy Idea Into A Global Brand. The Book Blends Personal Stories With Practical Insights—How Partnerships Were Formed, How The Company Culture Took Shape, And How Risks Were Weighed And Managed—Making Business Concepts Feel Human, Relatable, And Actionable. Honest, First-Person Storytelling That Traces Nike’S Origins From A Tiny Start To A Global Brand Behind-The-Scenes Look At Partnerships, Supply Chains, And The Teams That Built The Company Entrepreneurial Lessons On Resilience, Risk-Taking, Focus, And Leadership Engaging Narrative Style With Humor, Humility, And Vivid Scenes Accessible Exploration Of Bootstrapping, Branding, And Company Culture After Finishing Shoe Dog, Readers Gain Practical Insights For Turning A Dream Into Reality, Plus A Renewed Belief In Perseverance, Collaboration, And The Power Of Vision. It Leaves You Inspired To Pursue Your Own Path With Confidence, And It Stays With You Long After The Last Page, Nudging You To Act On Your Ideas With Courage And Curiosity.
works.authorDescription:
Philip Hampson Knight (born February 24, 1938) is an American billionaire businessman who is the co-founder and chairman emeritus of Nike, Inc., a global sports footwear, equipment and apparel company. He was previously its chairman and CEO. As of October 2025, Forbes estimated his net worth at US$35.4 billion. He is also the owner of the stop motion film production company Laika. Knight is a graduate of the University of Oregon and the Stanford Graduate School of Business. He was part of the track and field club under coach Bill Bowerman at the University of Oregon with whom he would later co-found Nike.
Knight has donated hundreds of millions of dollars to each of his alma maters, as well as Oregon Health & Science University.

works.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
works.author: Stephen Covey
works.description: The 7 Habits Of Highly Effective People - Offers A Practical, Principled Path To Personal And Professional Growth. This Timeless Guide Is Perfect For Professionals, Leaders, Teachers, Students, And Parents Who Want Clear, Actionable Steps To Improve Focus, Productivity, And Character. The Tone Is Hopeful, Empowering, And Grounded, Inviting Readers To Build A Meaningful, Effective Life. Built Around Seven Enduring Habits, The Book Presents A Principle-Centered Approach To Influence, Renewal, And Everyday Decision-Making. The 30Th Anniversary Edition Adds Fresh Insights From Sean Covey, Connecting The Classic Lessons To Today’S Fast-Paced World. You’Ll Discover A Clear, Step-By-Step Pathway To Adapt To Change, Manage Your Energy, And Lead With Integrity, Fairness, And Human Dignity. Principle-Centered Framework For Personal And Professional Effectiveness The Seven Habits With Practical Guidance And Real-World Applications Updated 30Th Anniversary Edition With New Insights From Sean Covey Engaging Anecdotes And A Steady, Accessible Pace That Makes Concepts Stick Tools For Self-Renewal, Resilience, And Burnout Prevention Reading The 7 Habits Of Highly Effective People Leaves You With A Durable Blueprint For Lifelong Growth, A Calmer Sense Of Purpose, And The Confidence To Lead With Integrity In Any Setting. It Offers Lasting Value By Turning Timeless Wisdom Into Everyday Actions, Helping You Think Bigger, Act Cleaner, And Stay Committed To Your Best Self.
works.authorDescription: Stephen Richards Covey was an American educator, author, businessman, and speaker. His most popular book is The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. His other books include First Things First, Principle-Centered Leadership, The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Families, The 8th Habit, and The Leader In Me: How Schools and Parents Around the World Are Inspiring Greatness, One Child at a Time. In 1996, Time magazine named him one of the 25 most influential people. He was a professor at the Jon M. Huntsman School of Business at Utah State University (USU) at the time of his death.

works.title: The Autobiography of Malcolm X
works.author: Malcolm X with Alex Haley
works.description: The Autobiography of Malcolm X is an autobiography written by Muslim American minister and activist Malcolm X in collaboration with American journalist Alex Haley. It was released posthumously on October 29, 1965, nine months after his assassination.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Catch-22
works.author: Joseph Heller
works.description: Catch-22’ Is A Revolutionary Book By Joseph Heller Which Was First Published In 1961. This Book Is A One Of Its Kind. Heller Uses A Non-Chronological Third Person Omniscient Narration To Bind The Threads Together. Ideas Flow Into Each Other Through Random Connections Within The Story. Events Have Been Repeated Through Different Point Of Views. The Story Is Situated In The Time Of World War 2. This Story Is About The Life Of Captain John Yossarian, A U.S. Army Air Forces Bombardier In 256Th Squadron Who Has Been Assigned To Bomb Enemy Posts At Eastern France And Italy. The Phrase ‘Catch-22’ Was Later Added In English Language Referring To A Type Of Impossible Logic Puzzle Sometimes Called A Double Bind. According To This Story Unstable Men Do Not Have To Fly Aircrafts, But The Fact That They Can Rationally Decide For Themselves And Ask For Waiver, Proves That They Are Stable Enough. Yossarian Is The Lead Character Of This Story. A Man Who Is Afraid Of His Own Commanding Officers Because He Thinks That They Want To Kill Him, By Making Him Work More While All He Wants Is To Escape From The Situation. He Has Seen His Friends Dying And A Lot More Destruction. He Wants To Quit, But He Can't. The Story Is Quite Unique In Its Narration. Many Times In This Story, Jokes Are Completed Through Different Point Of View. This Is A Satirical Novel. If You Are Looking For A Piece Of Writing That Is Complex And Humorous, Pick This One.
works.authorDescription: Joseph Heller was an American author of novels, short stories, plays, and screenplays. His best-known work is his debut novel Catch-22 (1961), a satire on war and bureaucracy, whose title has become a synonym for an absurd or contradictory choice. He was nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature twice, in 1972 and 1975.

works.title: The Myth of the Strong Leader
works.author: Archie Brown
works.description: In this magisterial and wide-ranging survey of political leadership over the past hundred years, Archie Brown challenges the widespread belief that strong leaders - those who dominate their colleagues and the policy-making process - are the most successful and admirable.
