works.title: Bharat mein Isai Dharm-Prachartantra
works.author: Arun Shourie
works.description: A critical look at the history, methods, and political implications of Christian missionary activities in India.(Missionaries in India: Continuities, Changes, Dilemmas) प्रसिद्ध लेखक, पत्रकार और राजनेता अरुण शौरी द्वारा लिखित एक चर्चित और आलोचनात्मक पुस्तक है, जिसे वाणी प्रकाशन (Vani Prakashan) ने प्रकाशित किया है।
works.authorDescription: Arun Shourie is an Indian economist, journalist, author, and politician who has received the Ramon Magsaysay Award.

works.title: Surrender
works.author: Bono
works.description: The deeply personal memoir of U2's frontman, tracing his life from Dublin through his decades of global fame and activism.
works.authorDescription:
Paul David Hewson (born 10 May 1960), known by the nickname Bono ( BON-oh), is an Irish singer-songwriter and activist. He is a founding member, the lead vocalist, and primary lyricist of the rock band U2. Bono is known for his impassioned vocal style as well as his grandiose songwriting and performance style. His lyrics frequently include social and political themes, and religious imagery inspired by his Christian faith. 
Born and raised in Dublin, Ireland, he attended Mount Temple Comprehensive School where in 1976 he began dating his future wife, Alison Stewart, as well as forming, with schoolmates, the band that became U2. During U2's early years, Bono's lyrics contributed to the group's rebellious and spiritual tone. As the band matured, his lyrics became inspired more by personal experiences shared with the other members. As a member of U2, Bono has received 22 Grammy Awards and has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Aside from his music, Bono is an activist for s...

works.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
works.author: Gabriel Garcia Marquez
works.description: One Hundred Years Of Solitude Is A Sweeping Magical Realism Novel That Follows The Buendía Family Across Seven Generations In The Mythical Town Of Macondo. A Cornerstone Of Latin American Literature, This Deeply Imaginative Story Blends History, Myth, And Memory To Reveal How Cycles Of Fortune And Doom Shape Nations And Individuals Alike. Perfect For Readers Who Savor Lush Prose, Enduring Family Sagas, And Big Ideas, This Book Carries An Adventurous, Evocative Tone That Stays With You Long After You Turn The Last Page. In One Hundred Years Of Solitude , The Story Unfolds In A Voice That Blends Documentary Detail With Dreamlike Illumination. The Novel Is Written As An Expansive Family Chronicle Set Within Macondo, A Town That Becomes A Living Symbol For New Worlds And Their Foibles. The Rhythm Shifts Between Intimate Scenes Of Love, Fear, And Ambition And Sweeping Episodes Of History That Reveal How Passion And Obsession Can Echo Across Generations. The Experience Is Rich With Magical Realism, Where Ghosts, Prophecies, And Miraculous Events Sit Beside Ordinary Daily Life, Inviting Readers To Slow Down, Question Certainty, And Notice The Patterns That Connect Distant Moments. Written With Luminous, Precise Prose, The Book Invites Careful Rereading As Motifs And Symbols Repeat And Evolve. The Journey Spans Landscapes Of Memory And Myth, Offering A Window Into Latin American History And Universal Questions About Fate, Memory, And The Human Longing To Leave A Mark. Epic Seven-Generation Saga Of The Buendía Family In Macondo Magical Realism Interwoven With History, Memory, And Prophecy Lyrical, Immersive Writing That Rewards Careful Rereading Themes Of History Repeating, Obsession, Fate, And Resilience Translated From Spanish Into 37 Languages, With A Global Readership After Finishing One Hundred Years Of Solitude , Readers Gain A Deeper Appreciation For History’S Cycles And The Enduring Resilience Of The Human Spirit. The Novel Lingers Like A Dream, Inviting Reflection On Memory, Community, And The Lasting Impact Of A Single Generation’S Choices.
works.authorDescription:
Gabriel José García Márquez (Latin American Spanish: [ɡaˈβɾjel ɣaɾˈsi.a ˈmaɾ.kes] ; 6 March 1927 – 17 April 2014) was a Colombian writer and journalist, known affectionately as Gabo ([ˈɡaβo]) or Gabito ([ɡaˈβito]) throughout Latin America. Considered one of the most significant authors of the 20th century, particularly in the Spanish language, he was awarded the 1972 Neustadt International Prize for Literature and the 1982 Nobel Prize in Literature. He pursued a self-directed education that resulted in leaving law school for a career in journalism. From early on he showed no inhibitions in his criticism of Colombian and foreign politics. In 1958, he married Mercedes Barcha Pardo; they had two sons, Rodrigo and Gonzalo.
García Márquez started as a journalist and wrote many acclaimed non-fiction works and short stories. He is best known for his novels, such as No One Writes to the Colonel (1961); One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967), which has sold over fifty million copies worldwide; Ch...

works.title: How to Change Your Mind
works.author: Michael Pollan
works.description: How to Change Your Mind: What the New Science of Psychedelics Teaches Us About Consciousness, Dying, Addiction, Depression, and Transcendence is a 2018 book by Michael Pollan. It became a No. 1 New York Times best-seller.
works.authorDescription:
Michael Kevin Pollan (; born February 6, 1955) is an American journalist, specializing in food, who is a professor and the first Lewis K. Chan Arts Lecturer at Harvard University. Concurrently, he is the Knight Professor of Science and Environmental Journalism and the director of the Knight Program in Science and Environmental Journalism at the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism, where in 2020 he cofounded the UC Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics, in which he leads the public-education program.
Pollan is best known for his books that explore the sociocultural effects of food, such as The Botany of Desire (2001) and The Omnivore's Dilemma (2006), as well as books that explore the effect of drugs on society and consciousness, such as How to Change Your Mind (2018) and This Is Your Mind On Plants (2021).
The popularity of his books has led to widespread awareness about various parts of the food system, including the local food movement, understanding the connections b...

works.title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
works.author: Bill Bryson
works.description: Travel Through Time And Space With A Really Short History Of Nearly Everything , A Playful, Kid-Friendly Exploration Of Science And The Story Of How We Came To Understand The World. This Engaging Adaptation Of Bryson's Classic Invites Readers From Ages 8 To 80 To Witness The Universe’S Grand Sweep—From The Big Bang To The Dawn Of Science—Through Bright Illustrations, Warm Humor, And Clear, Approachable Explanations. If You Crave Wonder, Curiosity, And A Dash Of Adventure, This Book Is For You. Written In A Breezy, Conversation Style, The Book— A Really Short History Of Nearly Everything —Moves With Short, Vivid Chapters That Jump From Planet Formation To The Curious Facts That Light Up Every Page. It Combines Storytelling With Accessible Lessons, So Big Ideas About Atoms, Dinosaurs, Oceans, And The Scale Of The Cosmos Become Inviting Puzzles Rather Than Intimidating Chapters From A Textbook. The Journey From A Single Cell To A Thriving Civilization Unfolds With Humor, Care, And A Deep Respect For The Scientists Who Bravely Asked Questions And Searched For Answers. Whether You're Reading Solo Or Sharing With A Curious Young Reader, The Structure Supports Exploration At Your Own Pace: Engaging Prose, Thoughtful Diagrams, And Plenty Of Moments To Pause, Wonder, And Discuss What It Means To Know Something. The Book Honors Science As An Evolving Story—Full Of Triumphs, Twists, And Surprising Connections—So Learning Feels Like A Fascinating Discovery Rather Than A Lecture. With The Warm, Bryson-Inspired Voice And A Really Short History Of Nearly Everything At The Center, This Adventure Makes Science Feel Accessible To Every Reader. Broad, Kid-Friendly Tour Of Science History From The Big Bang To Modern Discoveries Stunning Full-Color Illustrations That Bring Planets, Fossils, And Experiments To Life Short, Lively Chapters With Humor And Clear, Accessible Explanations Engaging Coverage Of Key Concepts: Atoms, Evolution, The Oceans, Dinosaurs, And More Spotlight On The Scientists Behind Breakthroughs, With Memorable Anecdotes Fun Facts And Thought-Provoking Questions That Spark Curiosity And Critical Thinking Warm, Inviting Prose That Echoes Bill Bryson’S Engaging Storytelling After Finishing A Really Short History Of Nearly Everything , Readers Gain A Sense Of Wonder And A Drive To Keep Asking Questions, Confident That Science Is A Lifelong Adventure That Starts At Home And Grows With Them.
works.authorDescription:
William McGuire Bryson ( BRYE-sən; born 8 December 1951) is an American journalist and author who was naturalized as a British citizen in 2014. Bryson has written nonfiction books on topics including travel, the English language, and science. Bryson moved to Britain in his twenties and remained in the country for most of his adult life. However, he periodically returned to live in the U.S. such as between 1995 and 2003. He was the chancellor of Durham University from 2005 to 2011.
In 1995, while in the United Kingdom, Bryson wrote Notes from a Small Island, an exploration of Britain. In 2003, he authored A Short History of Nearly Everything. In October 2020, he retired from writing books. He has sold over 16 million books worldwide. He recorded an audiobook for Audible, The Secret History of Christmas, in 2022.

works.title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
works.author: Charlie Munger
works.description: A comprehensive collection of the speeches, mental models, and investing wisdom of Berkshire Hathaway's Vice Chairman.
works.authorDescription: Charlie Munger was an American billionaire investor, businessman, and the closest partner of Warren Buffett.

works.title: Principles
works.author: Ray Dalio
works.description: Principles: Life And Work Distills Ray Dalio's Four Decades Of Experience Into A Practical Guide For Achieving Success In Life And Business. Part Memoir, Part Playbook, This Is Written For Students, Professionals, And Aspiring Leaders Who Want A Disciplined, Principle-Based Approach To Decision-Making. The Tone Is Thoughtful, Practical, And Inspiring, Inviting Readers To Adopt Radical Truth And Radical Transparency To Reach Meaningful Goals. In Principles: Life And Work , Dalio Lays Out The Core Ideas That Shaped Bridgewater Associates—From Idea Meritocracy To Radical Transparency. The Book Moves Through Clear, Actionable Steps And Real-World Examples, Showing How A Principled Framework Can Guide Tough Decisions, Build Stronger Teams, And Create Lasting Value. Readers Will Find Hundreds Of Practical Lessons Grounded In A Mindset That Favors Clarity, Curiosity, And Disciplined Experimentation. Written In A Warm, Engaging Voice, The Book Combines Storytelling With Practical Tools. You'll Discover How Dalio’S Innovations—Like Using Baseball Cards To Highlight Strengths And Weaknesses And Believability-Weighted Decision Processes—Translate To Everyday Work And Life. The Pace Balances Narrative With Method, Making Complex Concepts Approachable Whether You’Re New To Leadership Or Looking To Sharpen An Established Strategy. Core Concepts: Idea Meritocracy, Radical Truth, Radical Transparency, And Structured Decision-Making Practical Tools: Baseball Cards, Believability-Weighted Decisions, And Data-Driven Processes Learning Outcomes: Sharper Decisions, Stronger Teams, Clearer Goals Writing And Presentation: Clear, Applicable, Narrative-Driven After Finishing Principles: Life And Work , Readers Gain A Practical Blueprint They Can Apply Immediately To Decisions, Teams, And Everyday Challenges, Leaving With Greater Clarity, Confidence, And A Renewed Sense Of Purpose For Life And Work.
works.authorDescription: Raymond Thomas Dalio is an American billionaire investor and founder of Bridgewater Associates, one of the world's largest hedge funds.

works.title: Snow Crash
works.author: Neal Stephenson
works.description: A pioneering cyberpunk novel that predicted the 'Metaverse', following a hacker delivering pizzas in a hyper-capitalist future.
works.authorDescription: Neal Stephenson is an American speculative fiction writer known for his works blending technology, philosophy, and history.

works.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
works.author: Jared Diamond
works.recommendedBy: Bill Gates, Saurabh Dwivedi, Vikas Divyakirti (likely)
works.description: This Non-Fiction History Book Examines Why Civilizations Developed So Differently Around The World. Its Central Premise Is That Geography And Biogeography—More Than Race Or Culture—Shaped The Destinies Of Societies. It’S Written For Curious Readers, Students, And Lifelong Learners Who Want A Clear, Evidence-Based Look At Our Past. The Tone Is Thoughtful, Accessible, And Inspiring. Presented As A Sweeping Synthesis Of History, Biology, Ecology, And Linguistics, It Uses Maps, Diagrams, And Global Case Studies To Show How Environment And Resources Shaped Technology, Governance, And Trade. The Reading Experience Is Engaging And Accessible, Guiding Readers Through A Global Arc And Inviting Fresh Ways To Think About Humanity’S Development. Key Concepts Covered Include Domestication, Agriculture, Technology Diffusion, And The Role Of Disease In Shaping Civilizations. Geography And Biogeography As Drivers Of Civilization Global Case Studies Across Continents Technology Diffusion, Domestication, Agriculture, And Disease Impact Maps And Diagrams That Clarify Complex Ideas Accessible, Evidence-Based Narrative That Encourages Critical Thinking After Reading, You'll Have A Holistic Framework For Analyzing World History—Recognizing How Environment, Biology, And Human Ingenuity Intersect. The Work Supports Interactive Learning And Discussion, Builds Curiosity And Critical Thinking, And Offers A Broader Perspective On Today’S Global Challenges, Leaving A Thoughtful, Lasting Impression.
works.authorDescription: Jared Mason Diamond is an American scientist, historian, and author. He has written hundreds of scientific and popular articles and books, most notably Guns, Germs, and Steel (1997), which received multiple awards, including the 1998 Pulitzer Prize for general nonfiction. In 2005, Diamond was ranked ninth on a poll by Prospect and Foreign Policy of the world's top 100 public intellectuals.

works.title: Why Nations Fail
works.author: Acemoglu & Robinson
works.description: Why Nations Fail Explains Why Some Nations Prosper While Others Stay Poor, Arguing That Institutions—The Rules, Practices, And Norms That Shape Economic Life—Are The Primary Drivers Of Long‑Term Wealth. This Influential, Award‑Nominated Work Is Written For Curious Readers Of Economics, History, And Politics, As Well As Students Seeking A Clear, Big‑Picture Answer To Why Nations Succeed Or Falter. The Tone Is Thoughtful, Rigorous, And Accessible, Inviting Readers To Rethink Global Disparities With Confidence And Curiosity. Spanning Ancient Rome, Tudor England, And Modern China, Why Nations Fail Blends Historical Narrative With Contemporary Analysis To Present A Single, Persuasive Framework. The Authors Weave Case Studies With Data To Show How Inclusive Institutions—Where Power Is Dispersed And Property And Rights Are Protected—Fuel Investment, Innovation, And Peace, While Extractive Institutions Concentrate Power And Wealth And Often Hinder Growth. The Book Is Structured To Build A Practical Understanding: Complex Ideas Explained Through Engaging Examples, Clear Concepts, And A Pace That Keeps Real-World Relevance At The Forefront. If You Enjoy Thoughtful Blends Of History, Economics, And Political Science, This Work Offers A Compelling Journey Through The Forces That Shape Nations’ Destinies. Key Concepts : Inclusive Vs. Extractive Institutions, Property Rights, Rule Of Law, Political Accountability Standout Features : Cross‑Disciplinary Analysis, Rich Historical And Contemporary Case Studies, Evidence‑Based Arguments Learning Outcomes : Explains How Policy Choices Affect Growth, Development, And Long‑Term Prosperity Writing Style : Clear, Engaging, And Rigorously Argued, With Accessible Storytelling That Makes Complex Ideas Approachable After Finishing Why Nations Fail, Readers Gain A New Framework For Understanding Wealth And Poverty—One That Highlights The Importance Of Strong, Inclusive Institutions And The Incentives They Create. The Book Leaves You With A Clearer Sense Of How Policy, History, And Individual Action Intersect To Shape A Nation’S Future, Inspiring Thoughtful Dialogue About Prosperity And The Best Paths Toward Lasting Growth.
works.authorDescription: Author biography not found.

works.title: Barbarian Days
works.author: William Finnegan
works.description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning memoir that explores a lifelong obsession with surfing as a lens to understand the world.
works.authorDescription: William Finnegan is a staff writer at The New Yorker and the author of works of international journalism. He has specially addressed issues of racism and conflict in Southern Africa and politics in Mexico and South America, as well as poverty among youth in the United States, and is well known for his writing on surfing.

works.title: Midnight's Children
works.author: Salman Rushdie
works.description: Midnight's Children Is A Sweeping Magical Realism Novel About India's Birth And Its Ongoing Search For Identity. Set In Post-Colonial India, It Follows Saleem Sinai, Born At The Stroke Of Midnight On India's Independence, One Of 1,001 Children Linked By A Telepathic Bond. This Tale Appeals To Readers Who Enjoy Historical Fiction, Coming-Of-Age Stories, And Vibrant, Dreamlike Worlds. The Tone Is Intimate, Lyrical, And Thought-Provoking—Part History, Part Myth, Entirely Human. The Novel Is Written In A Lush, Panoramic Voice That Blends Intimate Memory With The Sweep Of A Nation’S History. It Moves Through Time With Shifting, Sometimes Playful Transitions, Anchored By Saleem's Life And His Telepathic Connections To His Fellow Midnight Children. The Experience Is Richly Immersive, Pairing Vivid Settings—From Crowded Cities To Quiet Family Rooms—With A Pace That Invites You To Linger Over A Line Of Dialogue Or A Scene Of Memory. Midnight's Children Uses Magic Realism To Explore Questions Of Power, Memory, And Belonging, Creating A World That Feels Both Fantastical And Deeply Real. In Midnight's Children, You Will Meet A Cast Of Unforgettable Characters And Traverse A Country Coming Into Its Own, As Saleem's Life Mirrors The Nation's Transformation. Epic Coming-Of-Age Tale Set Against Post-Independence India, Weaving Personal And National Histories Magical Realism Elements, Including The Telepathic Link Among The Midnight Children Rich, Lyrical Prose With A Panoramic, Decades-Spanning Timeline Layered Storytelling With Shifting Perspectives And A Memorable Cast Thought-Provoking Themes Of Identity, Fate, Freedom, And Belonging After Finishing Midnight's Children, Readers Gain A Deeper Understanding Of How Individual Lives Mirror A Nation’S Arc, And They Walk Away With A Sense Of Wonder About The Ties That Bind History To Memory. This Is A Book That Invites Reflection, Empathy, And A Lasting Appreciation For Storytelling That Merges The Personal With The Political.
works.authorDescription: Sir Ahmed Salman Rushdie is an Indian-born British and American novelist. His work often combines magical realism with historical fiction and primarily deals with connections, disruptions, and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations. His novels are typically set on the Indian subcontinent, feature an Indian protagonist, and/or portray Indian familial relationships. Rushdie's second novel, Midnight's Children (1981), won the Booker Prize in 1981 and was deemed to be "the best novel of all winners" on two occasions that marked the 25th and the 40th anniversary of the prize.

works.title: The Body Keeps the Score
works.author: Bessel van der Kolk
works.description: This Is A Comprehensive Non-Fiction Guide To Understanding Traumatic Stress And Healing. Drawing On More Than Thirty Years Of Clinical Work At A Renowned Trauma Center, It Blends Powerful Real‑World Case Histories With Accessible Neuroscience To Illuminate How Trauma Affects Body And Mind. Designed For Survivors, Family Members, Clinicians, And Students Seeking Clarity And Practical Pathways To Recovery, The Tone Is Compassionate, Evidence‑Based, And Hopeful. Content Is Presented As A Careful Synthesis Of Science And Lived Experience, Making Complex Ideas Approachable For A Broad Audience. Readers Move Through Material That Links Biology With Daily Feelings, Helping Them Make Sense Of Symptoms And Responses. Core Concepts Include The Neurobiology Of Trauma, Self‑Regulation, Attachment, Mindfulness, And Body‑Based Therapies, All Translated Into Practical Steps That Can Be Tried At Home Or With A Therapist. The Writing Is Clear And Human, With Concrete Examples That Illuminate How Healing Unfolds Over Time. Key Content Elements: Real‑World Case Histories, Explanations Of Brain And Nervous System Responses, And Practical Healing Strategies Grounded In Neuroscience And Clinical Practice Learning Outcomes: Deeper Understanding Of Trauma, Enhanced Self‑Regulation, And Improved Coping Skills For Daily Life Illustration Or Writing Style: Clear, Compassionate Prose That Blends Science With Personal Narrative Interactive Or Standout Features: Accessible, Step‑By‑Step Guidance That Invites Reflection And Application In Real Situations Readers Finish With A Clearer Map Of Trauma, A Sense Of Agency, And Practical Tools To Support Healing For Themselves And Others. It Builds Confidence, Sparks Curiosity, And Offers A Compassionate Perspective On Mental Health That Can Endure Long After The Last Page.
works.authorDescription: Bessel van der Kolk is a Boston-based Dutch-American psychiatrist, author, researcher and educator. Since the 1970s his research has been in the area of post-traumatic stress. He is the author of four books, including The New York Times best seller The Body Keeps the Score, which was translated into 43 languages. Scientists have criticized the book for promoting pseudoscientific claims about trauma, memory, the brain, and development.

works.title: Chip War
works.author: Chris Miller
works.description: Chip War Is A Gripping, Rigorous Look At How Microchip Technology Has Become Central To Global Power. Part History, Part Policy Study, This Book Traces The Way A Tiny Piece Of Silicon Reshaped Economies, Wars, And Diplomacy. Written For Curious Readers—From Students Of History And Technology To Policy Professionals And Business Leaders—Chip War Speaks With Urgency And Clarity About A Topic That Touches Everyday Life And Far-Flung Nations Alike. Chris Miller, An Economic Historian, Guides Readers Through A Narrative Built On Milestones In The Chip Race, Weaving Together The United States’ Long-Standing Leadership, Cold War Tensions, And The Current Surge Of Investment From China. The Book Reveals How Design Prowess, Fabrication Capability, And Complex Supply Chains Intersect With Policy And Strategy On The World Stage. The Experience Is Engaging: Crisp Chapters, Vivid Portraits Of Engineers And Decision-Makers, And Concrete Examples That Show Why A Supply Chain Decision Or A Single Fabrication Setback Can Shift The Balance Of Power. Chip War Makes Technical Ideas Accessible By Connecting Them To Real-World Consequences, Helping Readers See Technology As A Driver Of History Rather Than A Background Detail. The Result Is A Thoughtful, Timely Examination Of How A Global Technology Race Reshapes Economic And Military Landscapes—And Why Chip War Matters To Anyone Who Cares About The Future Of Power And Innovation. Key Content Elements: The Global Importance Of Microchips, Geopolitics, And Economic Influence Standout Features: Compelling Profiles Of Policymakers, Engineers, And Firms Shaping The Chip Landscape Learning Experiences: Clear Explanations Of Semiconductor Design, Fabrication, And Supply Chains Writing And Style: Narrative-Driven History That Reads Like A Thriller Yet Stays Rigorously Grounded By The End, Readers Will Gain A Clearer Understanding Of Why Chip War Matters In Everyday Life And Global Affairs. They’Ll Come Away With A Sharper Sense Of How Technology, Policy, And Power Intertwine, And How Today’S Decisions Could Redefine The Future Of Innovation And Security.

works.title: The Splendid and the Vile
works.author: Erik Larson
works.description: A cinematic history of Winston Churchill's first year as Prime Minister, focusing on his leadership during the London Blitz.
works.authorDescription: Erik Larson is a master of narrative nonfiction and a bestselling American author.

works.title: Meri Jeevan Yatra
works.author: Rahul Sankrityayan
works.description: Step Into The World Of Saadat Hasan Manto With Manto Selected Short Stories - , A Piercing Collection Of Urdu Tales That Illuminate The Human Heart Under Pressure. These Stories, Rooted In Mid-20Th-Century India And The Partition Era, Blend Stark Realism With Emotional Depth. Ideal For Adult Readers, Students Of Literature, And Anyone Drawn To Fearless, Human-Centered Storytelling, The Collection Carries An Urgent, Emotionally Honest Tone That Feels Both Provocative And Enduring. Each Story Is A Tightly Crafted Window Into Everyday Life—Often Shocking, Sometimes Tender. The New Translation In This Edition Preserves Manto's Crisp Cadence, Letting High Emotion And Concise Narration Coexist. The Book's Structure Gathers A Curated Set Of Tales That Move From Intimate Character Sketches To Broader Social Portraiture, Jumping Between Bustling City Streets And Wounded Margins. The Experience Is Immersive: You Sense The Tension, The Moral Ambiguity, And The Raw Honesty At The Core Of Manto's Voice. If You Love Fiction That Lingers, You Will Remember Unforgettable Characters—A Dhobi Who Unexpectedly Becomes A Killer, A Child-Like Prostitute Navigating A Brutal World—And You Will Feel The Climate Of Fear, Longing, And Resilience That Runs Through Partition-Era Stories. The Prose Is Accessible Yet Piercing, Inviting Reflection Without Sermonizing, And It Rewards Patient, Attentive Reading. A Curated Selection Of Manto's Most Impactful Short Stories New Translation Preserving Rhythm, Intensity, And Nuance Unforgettable Characters From City Life To Wartime Margins Themes Of Love, Loss, Survival, And Partition-Era Social Realities Concise, Piercing Storytelling With High Emotional Stakes Accessible Prose That Invites Reflection And Empathy After Finishing Manto Selected Short Stories - , Readers Gain A Deeper Understanding Of The Complexities Of Human Emotion, Empathy For Those Living On The Margins, And A Renewed Appreciation For Urdu Storytelling. The Collection Lingers, Inviting You To Reconsider Violence, Courage, And Everyday Moral Choices Long After The Last Page.
works.authorDescription: Saadat Hasan Manto NI was a Pakistani writer, playwright and novelist from Punjab, who is regarded as the greatest short-story author in Urdu literature. He was active from 1933 during British rule till his death in 1955 after independence.

works.title: Manto Dastavez
works.author: Saadat Hasan Manto
works.description: The monumental autobiography of one of India's greatest polymaths and travelers, detailing his journeys across Asia.
works.authorDescription: Rahul Sankrityayan is called the 'Father of Hindi Travel literature' and was a prominent Indian Marxist and Buddhist scholar.

works.title: The Power Broker
works.author: Robert Caro
works.description: This is the first and foremost a brilliant multidimensional portrait of a man-an extraordinary man who, denied power within the normal framework of the democratic process, stepped outside that framework to grasp power sufficient to shape a great city and hold sway over the very texture of millions of lives.

works.title: The Master and His Emissary
works.author: Iain McGilchrist
works.description: A new edition of the bestselling classic—published with a special introduction to mark its 10th anniversary This pioneering account sets out to understand the structure of the human brain – the place where mind meets matter. Until recently, the left hemisphere of our brain has been seen as the ‘rational’ side, the superior partner to the right. But is this distinction true? Drawing on a vast body of experimental research, Iain McGilchrist argues while our left brain makes for a wonderful servant, it is a very poor master. As he shows, it is the right side which is the more reliable and insightful. Without it, our world would be mechanistic – stripped of depth, colour and value.

works.title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
works.author: Douglas Hofstadter
works.description: A scientist and mathematician explores the mystery and complexity of human thought processes from an interdisciplinary point of view

works.title: Chaos: Making a New Science
works.author: James Gleick
works.description: The “highly entertaining” New York Times bestseller, which explains chaos theory and the butterfly effect, from the author of The Information (Chicago Tribune). For centuries, scientific thought was focused on bringing order to the natural world. But even as relativity and quantum mechanics undermined that rigid certainty in the first half of the twentieth century, the scientific community clung to the idea that any system, no matter how complex, could be reduced to a simple pattern. In the 1960s, a small group of radical thinkers began to take that notion apart, placing new importance on the tiny experimental irregularities that scientists had long learned to ignore. Miniscule differences in data, they said, would eventually produce massive ones—and complex systems like the weather, economics, and human behavior suddenly became clearer and more beautiful than they had ever been before. In this seminal work of scientific writing, James Gleick lays out a cutting edge field of science with enough grace and precision that any reader will be able to grasp the science behind the beautiful complexity of the world around us. With more than a million copies sold, Chaos is “a groundbreaking book about what seems to be the future of physics” by a writer who has been a finalist for both the Pulitzer Prize and the National Book Award, the author of Time Travel: A History and Genius: The Life and Science of Richard Feynman (Publishers Weekly).

works.title: Bose: The Untold Story of an Inconvenient Nationalist
works.author: Chandrachur Ghose
works.description: Bose: The Untold Story Of An Inconvenient Nationalist* Is A Deeply Researched Biography That Invites Readers Into The Life Of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, One Of India's Most Influential Freedom Fighters. This Non-Fiction Account Navigates The Freedom Movement With Clarity And Nuance—From His Resignation From The Indian Civil Service To Bold Challenges To Gandhian Leadership And His Controversial Exile—Offering A Fresh, Balanced Portrait For History Enthusiasts, Students, And Curious Readers. The Tone Blends Respect With Rigorous Inquiry, Delivering An Engaging And Contemplative Journey Through A Pivotal Era. Written As An Expansive, Revelatory Portrait, Bose: The Untold Story Of An Inconvenient Nationalist* Weaves Together Dramatic Episodes, Careful Analysis, And Newly Surfaced Perspectives To Illuminate Lesser-Known Facets Of Bose’S Life. You’Ll Explore His Exile And The Formation Of Two Governments, His Intense Involvement With Revolutionary Networks, And His Relentless Pursuit To Unite A Country Divided By Communal Tensions. The Narrative Presents These Moments In An Accessible, Thoughtfully Paced Style That Invites Both Reflection And Curiosity. Beyond Politics, The Book Delves Into Bose’S Personal Relationships And Spiritual Leanings To Reveal A Multi-Dimensional Leader. It Also Examines Covert Operations And Efforts To Incite Rebellion Within The Indian Armed Forces, Along With The Sensitive Controversy Surrounding His Association With Axis Powers, All Presented In Context-Rich Detail. This Careful Approach Transforms What You Thought You Knew Into A Deeper, More Complex Story About Sacrifice, Vision, And The Enduring Questions Surrounding A Nation’S Struggle For Freedom. Comprehensive Coverage Of Bose’S Life, Including Exile And The Formation Of Two Governments. Insight Into Revolutionary Networks, National Unity Efforts, And Attempts To Bridge Communal Divides. Exploration Of Personal Relationships And Spiritual Beliefs Shaping His Leadership. Analysis Of Covert Operations And Controversial Ties To Axis Powers, Presented With Balanced Context. Clear, Engaging Narrative That Makes Intricate History Accessible And Thought-Provoking. Balanced Perspective That Invites Readers To Re-Evaluate Bose’S Legacy In India’S Freedom Story. After Finishing Bose: The Untold Story Of An Inconvenient Nationalist*, Readers Gain A Deeper, More Nuanced Understanding Of Bose’S Impact On India's Independence And The Questions His Life Raises About Leadership, Sacrifice, And National Identity. The Journey Leaves You With A Sense Of Wonder And A Clearer View Of How One Determined Person Helped Shape A Nation—And How History Continues To Illuminate Present-Day Choices.

works.title: Mrignayani & Ahilyabai
works.author: Vrindavan Lal Verma
works.description: Two classic Hindi historical novels celebrating the valor and leadership of prominent female figures from Indian history.
works.authorDescription: Vrindavan Lal Verma was an eminent Hindi novelist and playwright known for historical fiction based on the Bundelkhand region.

works.title: The Making of the President 1960
works.author: Theodore White
works.description: The revolutionary political journalism book that chronicled the 1960 election between John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon.
works.authorDescription: Theodore White was an American political journalist and historian who changed how presidential campaigns are reported.

works.title: Mastery
works.author: Robert Greene
works.description: This Non-Fiction Guide To Personal Development Blends Historical Biography With Practical Psychology To Show How Exceptional Achievement Is Built Through Disciplined Practice, Curiosity, And Breaking Free From Conventional Molds. It Speaks To Curious Adults, Students, And Professionals Who Want A Clear, Evidence-Based Path To Their Best Work, Delivering An Inspiring And Thoughtful Voice Without Pretense. Presented As A Narrative-Driven Analysis, The Book Weaves Compact Biographies With Field-Tested Ideas About Learning, Creativity, And Resilience. It Invites Readers To See How Early Setbacks Can Become Stepping Stones And How Deliberate Apprenticeship—Guided By Mentors, Feedback, And Steady Effort—Unlocks Hidden Potential. The Reading Experience Feels Approachable And Practical, With Concepts Explained In Plain Language And Real-World Examples That Invite Reflection And Action. Readers Move Through The Material By Identifying Their Own Passions, Mapping A Disciplined Apprenticeship, And Applying The Idea That Success Is Built From Consistent Practice And Curiosity. The Text Treats Peak Performance As A Process, Showing How To Dismantle Limiting Norms And Reconstruct Them To Fit Personal Goals. It Blends Storytelling With Actionable Steps, So Progress Feels Tangible Rather Than Theoretical. Biographical Case Studies And Practical Frameworks That Illuminate How World-Changing Outcomes Emerge From Focused Work Deliberate Practice, Feedback Loops, Goal-Setting, And Resilience As Core Skills For Lifelong Learning Reflective Prompts, Practical Exercises, And Templates To Design Your Own Apprenticeship Plan Story-Driven Explanations Paired With Clear, Accessible Writing To Support Understanding And Application Interactive Elements That Encourage You To Experiment, Adapt, And Persist Through Challenges By The End, Readers Gain A Practical Road Map To Pursue Their Own Path With Confidence, Curiosity, And Resilience. It Invites You To Take Control Of Your Learning Journey, Develop A Long-Term Practice, And Approach Challenges With A Fresh Perspective. The Book Leaves A Lasting Impression By Showing That Meaningful Achievement Comes From Living By Your Own Rules And Steadily Building The Skills You Care About.
works.authorDescription: Richard Greene is a Canadian poet. His book Boxing the Compass won the Governor General's Award for English language poetry at the 2010 Governor General's Awards.

works.title: Superintelligence
works.author: Nick Bostrom
works.description: Instant New York Times and USA Today Bestseller.Tech visionary and co-founder of Manas AI Reid Hoffman shares his unique insider’s perspective on an AI-powered future, making the case for its potential to unlock a world of possibilities.An essential companion. — Fei-Fei LiAn important read. —Bill GatesBrilliant mind. Compassionate heart. Bold ideas…Read this book!” —Van Jones Refreshingly optimistic and welcome perspective. — Ariana Huffington A fascinating and insightful book. —Yuval Noah HarariAs taught at UPenns Wharton and Stanford. Superagency offers a roadmap for using AI inclusively and adaptively to improve our lives and create positive change. While acknowledging challenges like disinformation and potential job changes, the book focuses on AI’s immense potential to increase individual agency and create better outcomes for society as a whole. Imagine AI tutors personalizing education for each child, researchers rapidly discovering cures for diseases like Alzheimers and cancer, and AI advisors empowering people to navigate complex systems and achieve their goals. Hoffman and co-author, tech and culture writer Greg Beato envision a world where these possibilities, and many more, become a reality.Superagency challenges conventional fears, inviting us to view the future through a lens of opportunity, rather than fear. It’s a call to action – to embrace AI with excitement and actively shape a world where human ingenuity and the power of AI combine to create something extraordinary.
works.authorDescription:
Nick Bostrom ( BOST-rəm; Swedish: Niklas Boström [ˈnɪ̌kːlas ˈbûːstrœm]; born 10 March 1973) is a philosopher known for his work on existential risk, the anthropic principle, human enhancement ethics, whole brain emulation, superintelligence risks, and the reversal test. He was the founding director of the later defunct Future of Humanity Institute at the University of Oxford and has become Principal Researcher at the Macrostrategy Research Initiative.
Bostrom is the author of Anthropic Bias: Observation Selection Effects in Science and Philosophy (2002), Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies (2014) and Deep Utopia: Life and Meaning in a Solved World (2024).
Bostrom believes that advances in artificial intelligence (AI) may lead to superintelligence, which he defines as "any intellect that greatly exceeds the cognitive performance of humans in virtually all domains of interest". He views this as a major source of opportunities and existential risks.

works.title: The Denial of Death
works.author: Ernest Becker
works.description: Dialogue With Death Invites You To Slow Down, Look Inward, And Explore What Makes Life Meaningful. This Contemplative Guide Blends Philosophy And Gentle Encouragement To Help Adults And Curious Readers Reflect On Big Questions—Why Are We Here? What Truly Matters?—And To Approach Each Day With Courage, Curiosity, And Hopeful Heart. Written As A Thoughtful Dialogue With Mortality, Dialogue With Death Unfolds In A Warm, Accessible Voice. The Book Is Structured Around Reflective Prompts, Short Chapters, And Meditative Exercises That Invite Brisk, Thoughtful Reading Or Longer, Meditative Sessions. Rather Than Preachiness, It Offers Practical Insight: Identify What You Value, Repair Strained Relationships, And Choose Actions That Honor The Moments You’Re Given. Key Concepts Such As Time As A Precious Resource, Living With Intention, Forgiveness, Gratitude, And Connection Are Presented In Clear, Approachable Language. Even When Tackling Heavy Ideas, The Tone Remains Uplifting, Turning Existential Questions Into Everyday Guidance That Makes Living Well Feel Within Reach. Core Themes Of Life, Death, And Meaning Explored With Warmth And Clarity Thought-Provoking Prompts, Questions, And Exercises To Guide Daily Choices Accessible Writing And A Gentle Structure That Makes Big Ideas Feel Personal Short, Meditative Chapters And Reflective Pacing For Flexible Reading Focus On Relationships, Gratitude, And Living With Intention To Create Lasting Impact After Finishing Dialogue With Death, You’Ll Carry A Refreshed Sense Of Purpose, A Calmer Appreciation For Each Moment, And A Commitment To Live With More Joy, Hope, And Love. It Offers A Welcoming Invitation To Celebrate Life’S Fragility And To Make Choices That Honor What Matters Most, Leaving You Inspired To Move Forward With Confidence.
works.authorDescription: Ernest Becker (September 27, 1924 – March 6, 1974) was an American cultural anthropologist and author of the 1973 Pulitzer Prize-winning book The Denial of Death.

works.title: Unbroken
works.author: Laura Hillenbrand
works.description: Unbroken: A World War II Story of Survival, Resilience, and Redemption is a 2010 non-fiction book by Laura Hillenbrand.
works.authorDescription:
Laura Hillenbrand (born May 15, 1967) is an American author. Her two bestselling nonfiction books, Seabiscuit: An American Legend (2001) and Unbroken: A World War II Story of Survival, Resilience, and Redemption (2010), have sold over 13 million copies, and each was adapted for film. Her writing style is distinct from New Journalism, dropping "verbal pyrotechnics" in favor of a stronger focus on the story itself.
Hillenbrand fell ill in college and was unable to complete her degree. She shared that experience in an award-winning essay, A Sudden Illness, published in The New Yorker in 2003. Her books were written while she was disabled by myalgic encephalomyelitis, also known as chronic fatigue syndrome. In a 2014 interview, Bob Schieffer said to Laura Hillenbrand: "To me your story – battling your disease... is as compelling as his (Louis Zamperini's) story."

works.title: Intertwined Lives: P.N. Haksar and Indira Gandhi
works.author: Jairam Ramesh
works.description: A detailed political biography exploring the intellectual and strategic relationship between Indira Gandhi and her most powerful advisor.
works.authorDescription: Jairam Ramesh is an Indian politician and author who has held multiple ministerial portfolios in the Government of India.

works.title: The Iliad
works.author: Homer
works.description: This is a timeless epic poem, presented in a modern-verse translation and issued as a deluxe edition for today’s readers. The central journey follows a legendary traveler as he faces divine beings, seascapes, and daunting challenges on a long voyage home after a great war. Aimed at adults, students of classics, and readers who love mythic storytelling, it carries an adventurous, lyrical, and contemplative tone that invites savoring the language and ideas. The content is presented as a story-driven narrative, with a readable translation that preserves energy and cadence while staying accessible. It includes a scholarly introduction and contextual notes that illuminate history, myth, and craft, helping readers—whether new to the classics or continuing study—gain context without interrupting the flow. The reading experience is immersive: vivid episodes, lyrical language, and evocative scenes make it a pleasure to read aloud or in quiet study. Readers move through the text with room for reflection, guided by the notes and the enduring questions the narrative raises about courage, cleverness, and resilience. Modern-verse translation that preserves cadence while staying accessible Story-driven narrative with vivid episodes and memorable scenes Scholarly introduction and contextual notes for deeper understanding Deluxe edition features French flaps and deckle-edged paper Read-aloud friendly language; suitable for classrooms and family reading Timeless themes of courage, wit, endurance, and leadership Readers finish with a deeper appreciation for ancient storytelling, enhanced critical and cultural insights, and a work that invites ongoing rereading, discussion, and personal growth.
works.authorDescription:
Homer (; Ancient Greek: Ὅμηρος [hómɛːros], Hómēros; possibly born c. 8th century BC) was an ancient Greek poet who is traditionally credited as the author of the Iliad and the Odyssey, two epic poems that are foundational works of ancient Greek literature. Homer was highly revered in ancient Greek society and is considered one of the most influential authors in history. Today, the question of Homer's identity and existence—dubbed the "Homeric Question"—continues to be debated, and scholars generally regard the two poems as the works of separate authors.
The Iliad centers on a quarrel between King Agamemnon and the warrior Achilles during the last year of the Trojan War. The Odyssey chronicles the ten-year journey of Odysseus, king of Ithaca, back to his home after the fall of Troy. The epics depict man's struggle, the Odyssey especially so, as Odysseus perseveres through the punishment of the gods. works.title: Baburnama
works.author: Babur
works.description: This is a historical non-fiction memoir in translation that offers an intimate, first-person view into the life of the founder of the Mughal Empire. It traces a ruler’s journey from a child on the throne to a monarch who shapes a vast realm, capturing the era’s politics, journeys, and daily life. Designed for history lovers, students, and curious readers, the tone blends educational insight with reflective, adventurous storytelling. Presented in its original Turki voice through a careful translation by Annette Susannah Beveridge, this complete life record invites readers to step inside the narrator’s world. The edition preserves the personal observations, candid reflections, and vivid descriptions that set this work apart as a rare autobiographical account in Islamic literature. Readers gain not only a chronology of campaigns and court life but also an intimate sense of geography, culture, and daily life across a diverse landscape. What makes the reading experience distinctive is the unfiltered, first-hand perspective—an autobiographical journey that blends memoir with history. The reader moves through episodes of war, diplomacy, travel, and governance, with the voice narrating realities of 16th-century Central and South Asia in a way that reads both like personal diary and broad chronicle. Complete life record from early ascent to power through establishment of the empire (1493–1529) First real autobiography in Islamic literature, offering a unique personal perspective Authentic Turki text rendered into a nuanced, faithful translation Rich historical and cultural context of 16th-century Central and South Asia, including geography, politics, and daily life Engaging, intimate narrative voice that blends memoir with historical insight By the end, readers gain a nuanced understanding of leadership, empire-building, and cross-cultural exchange. The work cultivates curiosity about early modern history, invites reflection on human ambition, and leaves a lasting impression of a remarkable voice from the past.
works.authorDescription:
Babur (Persian: ببر, Persian: [bɑː.βuɾ]; 14 February 1483 – 26 December 1530; born Zahīr ud-Dīn Muhammad) was the founder of the Mughal Empire in South Asia. He was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan through his father and mother, respectively. He was also given the posthumous name of Firdaws Makani ('Dwelling in Paradise').
Born in Andijan in the Fergana Valley (now in Uzbekistan), Babur was the eldest son of Umar Shaikh Mirza II (1456–1494, Timurid governor of Fergana from 1469 to 1494) and a great-great-great-grandson of Timur (1336–1405). He ascended the throne of Fergana in its capital, Akhsikath, in 1494 at the age of twelve and had to put down a rebellion. He conquered Samarkand two years later, only to lose Fergana soon after. In his attempt to reconquer Fergana, he lost control of Samarkand as well. In 1501, he briefly recaptured both areas but his attempt failed when the Uzbek prince Muhammad Shaybani defeated him and founded the Khanate of Bukhara.
In 1504, the exiled Ba...

works.title: How Prime Ministers Decide
works.author: Neerja Chowdhury
works.description: How Prime Ministers Decide Is A Rigorously Reported, Accessible Look At How India's Prime Ministers Shape History Through Their Most Consequential Choices. This Non-Fiction Political History In Invites Readers To Go Beyond Headlines And Into The Minds, Institutions, And Pressures That Guide Leadership In A Complex Democracy. Neerja Chowdhury Unpacks Six Pivotal Decisions, Offering A Clear-Eyed, Human Portrait Of The Leaders Who Steered The Nation At Critical Moments. It's A Thoughtful Read For Politics And History Enthusiasts, Students Of Governance, And Curious Readers Who Want To Understand The Craft Of Decision-Making. The Tone Is Educational Yet Engaging, Respectful Yet Quietly Suspenseful As Each Chapter Reveals How Chance, Timing, And Judgment Interact To Alter India's Course. How Prime Ministers Decide Is Structured Around Six Chapters, Each Centered On A Prime Minister And A Defining Decision. The Book Blends Interviews With Prime Ministers, Policymakers, And Influential Figures With Careful Archival Research, Presenting The Context, Constraints, And Consequences In A Readable, Narrative Style. This Approach Lets Readers See Not Just What Happened, But Why Decisions Unfolded The Way They Did, And What That Reveals About Leadership Under Pressure. In How Prime Ministers Decide, Chowdhury Moves Beyond Headlines To Illuminate The Human And Institutional Dynamics Behind A Democracy In Flux. Chowdhury’S Storytelling Feels Intimate Without Losing Rigor. The Writing Moves At A Steady Pace, Balancing Precise Analysis With Vivid Scenes From The Corridors Of Power, The Courtroom, And The Parliamentary Floor. Whether You’Re Drawn To Indira Gandhi's Tactical Comeback In 1980, Rajiv Gandhi's Controversial Choices, Or The Transformative Debates Around The Mandal Commission, The Babri Masjid Episode, Vajpayee’S Nuclear Shift, Or The Nuclear Deal Negotiated By Manmohan Singh, The Book Offers Clear Explanations Of Key Concepts—Political Strategy, Constitutional Constraints, And The Messy Realities Of Governing A Diverse Country. Six Pivotal Decisions That Shaped Modern India, Explored In Depth Profiles Of Six Prime Ministers And The Historical Contexts That Tested Their Leadership Based On Extensive Interviews With Prime Ministers, Officials, And Policymakers Narrative, Accessible Non-Fiction That Reads Like A Behind-The-Scenes Account Clear Analysis Of Strategic Thinking, Political Pressures, And Institutional Factors Written By Neerja Chowdhury, An Award-Winning Journalist And Political Commentator After Reading How Prime Ministers Decide, You’Ll Gain A Richer Understanding Of How Leadership Decisions Emerge In A Democracy, And You’Ll See The Subtle Interplay Between Timing, Counsel, And Institutions. This Book Helps Readers Think Differently About Politics And History, Offering Lasting Insights Into Governance And The Craft Of Decision-Making.
works.authorDescription: Neerja Chowdhury is an Indian journalist, columnist and political commentator. Chowdhury was the political editor of the Indian Express for ten years, and is currently a contributing editor for the Indian Express.

works.title: The Innovators
works.author: Walter Isaacson
works.description: The Innovators Is A Sweeping History By Walter Isaacson About The People Who Created The Computer And The Internet. Part Biography, Part Technology History, It Follows Innovators From Ada Lovelace To Tim Berners‑Lee And Larry Page, Revealing How Collaboration And Teamwork Turned Disruptive Ideas Into Everyday Technology. It’S Written For Curious Readers—Students, Professionals, And Lifelong Learners—Who Want An Engaging, Educational, And Inspiring Look At How The Digital Age Happened. Written In A Warm, Readable Voice, The Book Strings Together Biographical Portraits And Milestones, Organized Around The Idea That Teamwork Often Drives Breakthrough Invention. Isaacson Shows How Minds Across Generations And Disciplines Connected To Push Technology Forward, Weaving Personal Stories With Big Ideas. The Narrative Alternates Between Character-Driven Episodes And Broader Context, Keeping The Pace Lively While Making Complex Concepts Approachable. In The Innovators, You’Ll Meet Key Ideas—How Codes, Networks, And Platforms Emerged; The Social Dynamics And Collaboration Behind Innovation; And The Human Journeys Behind Landmark Breakthroughs. The Book Introduces A Gallery Of Memorable Figures And Settings While Delivering Practical Lessons About Creativity, Perseverance, And Teamwork. Biographical Portraits Of Ada Lovelace, Alan Turing, Bill Gates, Steve Jobs, Tim Berners‑Lee, And Other Pioneers Clear Explanations Of How Computing, Networking, And The Internet Evolved A Strong Emphasis On Collaboration And Teamwork As Engines Of Invention Engaging, Narrative-Driven Writing With Memorable Characters And Settings Accessible Explanations Of Key Concepts Such As Algorithms, Networks, And Platforms After Finishing The Innovators, Readers Gain A Clear Map Of The Digital Revolution, A Renewed Appreciation For Teamwork, And Ideas They Can Apply To Their Own Creative Projects. It Leaves You Inspired To Explore, Connect, And Build Together—Proof That Big Ideas Often Come To Life Through Collaboration.
works.authorDescription:
Walter Seff Isaacson (born May 20, 1952) is an American journalist who has written biographies of Henry Kissinger, Benjamin Franklin, Leonardo da Vinci, Albert Einstein, Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna, and Elon Musk. As of 2024, Isaacson is a professor at Tulane University and, since 2018, an interviewer for the PBS and CNN news show Amanpour & Company.
He has been the president and CEO of the Aspen Institute, a nonpartisan policy studies organization based in Washington, D.C., the chair and CEO of CNN, and the editor of Time.
Isaacson attended Harvard University and Pembroke College, Oxford as a Rhodes scholar. He is the co-author with Evan Thomas of The Wise Men: Six Friends and the World They Made (1986) and the author of Pro and Con (1983), Kissinger: A Biography (1992), Benjamin Franklin: An American Life (2003), Einstein: His Life and Universe (2007), American Sketches (2009), Steve Jobs (2011), The Innovators: How a Group of Hackers, Geniuses, and Geeks Created the Digital Revo...

works.title: Ethics
works.author: Baruch Spinoza
works.description: Non-Fiction Guide For Curious Minds, This Accessible Ethics Exploration Invites Readers To Grapple With Big Questions About Choice, Identity, And Duty In A World Marked By Historical Tragedies And Ongoing Injustices. The Central Aim Is To Help Readers Think Clearly About How Individual Actions Ripple Through Society And How Concepts Like Rights, Self-Interest, And Civic Responsibility Intersect In Our Time. Built For Adult Readers, Students, And Lifelong Learners, It Supports Interactive Learning And Invites Thoughtful Discussion In A Calm, Serious, And Hopeful Tone. Content Is Organized Into Concise Chapters That Blend Plain Explanations With Short Scenarios And Reflective Prompts. While Grounded In Philosophy, The Language Remains Accessible And The Visuals Provide Supportive Illustrations To Aid Understanding, Making It An Educational Book For Readers New To Philosophy. What Makes The Reading Experience Distinctive Is The Mix Of Real-World Examples And Guided Prompts That Invite Readers To Examine Their Own Beliefs And Practice Civil Dialogue. Readers Move Through The Content By Reading, Pausing To Reflect, And Engaging With Prompts That Support Activity-Based Learning And Can Be Used Solo Or In Discussion Groups. For Learners, The Book Covers Essential Concepts Such As Autonomy, Rights, Civic Duties, Identity, Nationalism, And The Tension Between Self-Interest And The Common Good. The Approach Makes Difficult Ideas Feel Accessible Through Clear Definitions, Real-World Contexts, And Approachable Explanations That Invite Ongoing Curiosity Rather Than Doctrinaire Certainty. Key Topics And Questions : Autonomy, Rights, Duties, Identity, Nationalism, And The Tension Between Self-Interest And The Common Good; Real-World Scenarios To Illustrate Concepts. The Book Aims To Leave Readers Thoughtful, Informed, And Ready To Continue Exploring How Ethics Guides Personal Choices And Public Responsibilities.
works.authorDescription:
Baruch (de) Spinoza (24 November 1632 – 21 February 1677), also known under his Latinized pen name Benedictus de Spinoza, was a philosopher of Portuguese-Jewish origin who was born and lived in the Dutch Republic. A forerunner of the Enlightenment, Spinoza significantly influenced modern biblical criticism, 17th-century rationalism, and Dutch intellectual culture, establishing himself as one of the most important and radical philosophers of the early modern period. Influenced by Stoicism, Thomas Hobbes, René Descartes, and heterodox Christians, Spinoza was a leading philosopher of the Dutch Golden Age.
Spinoza was born in Amsterdam to a Marrano family that fled Portugal for the more tolerant Dutch Republic. He received a traditional Jewish education, learning Hebrew and studying sacred texts within the Portuguese-Jewish community, where his father was a prominent merchant. As a young man, Spinoza challenged rabbinic authority and questioned Jewish doctrines, leading to his permanent ex...

works.title: The Black Swan
works.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
works.description: The Black Swan Is Nassim Nicholas Taleb's Provocative Examination Of Luck, Uncertainty, And The Unpredictable Events That Shape Our World. Part Philosophy, Part Practical Guide, This Non-Fiction Work Speaks To Readers Across Professions Who Want To Rethink Forecasting And Risk. Whether You’Re A Business Professional, A Student, Or Simply Curious About How Reality Really Behaves, The Black Swan Offers A Thoughtful, Accessible, And Sometimes Playful Invitation To Embrace Uncertainty Rather Than Fear It. Structured As A Series Of Ideas And Examples, The Black Swan Blends Rigorous Inquiry With A Conversational Voice That Makes Complex Ideas Approachable. Taleb Uses Real-World Stories—From Financial Crises To Cultural Phenomena Like The Rise Of Harry Potter And The Invention Of The Internet—To Illustrate How Rare Events Resist Prediction And How Post-Hoc Explanations Can Mislead Us. The Experience Is As Much About Shifting How You Think As About What You Think, With A Pace That Lets You Grapple With Big Questions Without Getting Lost In Jargon. Key Content Elements: The Concept Of Black Swan Events, Uncertainty, Limits Of Prediction, And Lessons For Risk Management Interactive Or Standout Features: Engaging Storytelling, Real-World Examples, Accessible Explanations Learning Outcomes Or Experiences: Rethink Forecasting, Learn To Anticipate The Unexpected, Improve Decision‑Making Under Uncertainty Writing Or Illustration Style: Lucid, Conversational, Thought-Provoking After Finishing The Black Swan, Readers Carry A New Lens To Evaluate Surprises And Plan For The Improbable. They Feel Equipped To Navigate Uncertainty With Curiosity And Resilience, Turning Rare Events Into Opportunities For Smarter Choices And Calmer, More Considered Thinking.

works.authorDescription: Bhalchandra Vanaji Nemade is an Indian Marathi language writer, poet, critic and linguistic scholar. Beginning with his debut novel Kosala, Nemade brought new dimensions to the world of Marathi literature. This was followed by a tetralogy consisting of novels Bidhar, Hool, Jareela and Jhool. In 2013, Nemade published his magnum opus titled Hindu: Jagnyachi Samruddha Adgal which is regarded as his masterpiece. Nemade is a recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award as well as the Jnanapith Award, the highest literary honour in India. In 2013, he was awarded the Padma Shri.

works.title: Savarkar
works.author: Vikram Sampath
works.description: Savarkar - Is A Sweeping, Meticulously Researched Portrait Of Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, One Of India's Most Controversial Figures, And The Concluding Volume In The Acclaimed Savarkar Series. Authored By Renowned Historian Vikram Sampath, The Book Delves Into The Complexities Of Savarkar's Life, His Evolving Ideas, And The Lasting Impact On India's Political Landscape. Written For History Lovers, Students Of Politics, And Curious Readers Seeking A Nuanced View Of Modern India, It Pairs Thoughtful Analysis With A Measured, Respectful Tone That Invites Reflection. Structured As A Narrative That Blends Biography With Political Analysis, The Book Moves Through Savarkar's Public Life And The Ideas That Shaped His Era While Weighing Competing Interpretations. The Prose Is Accessible And Engaging, Guiding Readers Through Controversial Questions—Was Savarkar Involved In Gandhi's Assassination, And What Were The Consequences For Communities In The Aftermath—Without Shying From Nuance. Sampath's Rigorous Scholarship Anchors The Discussion In Documented History And Presents The Evolution From Early Calls For Unity To The Rise Of Hindutva And The Politics Of The Hindu Mahasabha With Clarity And Balance. Comprehensive, Source-Based Examination Of Savarkar's Life, Politics, And Legacy Explores Gandhi's Assassination Debate And Its Aftermath For Communities Traces Savarkar's Shift From Hindu-Muslim Unity To Hindutva And Leadership In The Hindu Mahasabha Rigorous Historical Analysis By Vikram Sampath, Grounded In Archival Research Clear, Engaging Prose That Makes Dense History Accessible To General Readers By The End, Savarkar - Leaves Readers With A Nuanced Understanding Of How Identity, Ideology, And Power Shape Modern Indian History, Inviting Thoughtful Reflection On Political Legacies And Their Present-Day Echoes.
works.authorDescription: Vikram Sampath is an Indian popular historian and columnist, who is noted for writing biographies of Gauhar Jaan, Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Mysore Kings.

works.title: Steve Jobs
works.author: Walter Isaacson
works.description: Icon Takes A Look At The Most Astounding Figure In A Business Era Noted For Its Mavericks, Oddballs, And Iconoclasts. Drawing On A Wide Range Of Sources, Jeffrey Young And William Simon Provide New Perspectives On The Legendary Creation Of Apple, Detail Jobs’S Meteoric Rise, And The Devastating Plunge That Left Him Not Only Out Of Apple, But Out Of The Computer-Making Business Entirely. This Unflinching And Completely Unauthorized Portrait Reveals Both Sides Of Jobs’S Role In The Remarkable Rise Of The Pixar Animation Studio, Also Re-Creates The Acrimony Between Jobs And Disney’S Michael Eisner, And Examines Jobs’S Dramatic His Rise From The Ashes With His Recapture Of Apple. The Authors Examine The Takeover And Jobs’S Reinvention Of The Company With The Popular Imac And His Transformation Of The Industry With The Revolutionary Ipod. Icon Is Must Reading For Anyone Who Wants To Understand How The Modern Digital Age Has Been Formed, Shaped, And Refined By The Most Influential Figure Of The Age–A Master Of Three Industries: Movies, Music, And Computers.
works.authorDescription: Walter Seff Isaacson is an American journalist who has written biographies of Henry Kissinger, Benjamin Franklin, Leonardo da Vinci, Albert Einstein, Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna, and Elon Musk. Part Science, Part Biography, Part Detective Story, It Traces The Discovery And Meaning Of The Gene Across Centuries And Continents For Curious Readers Who Want To Understand How Heredity Shapes Who We Are. With An Earnest, Intimate Tone, The Gene Invites Science Lovers, History Buffs, And Lifelong Learners To Explore How Our Master-Code Has Reshaped Medicine, Ethics, And Even The Idea Of Free Will. Written As A Seamless Narrative, The Gene Moves From The 1856 Discovery In An Obscure Abbey To The Laboratories And Breakthroughs Of Mendel, Darwin, Crick, And Rosalind Franklin. Siddhartha Mukherjee Blends Rigorous Scholarship With Storytelling, Weaving Biographies, Historical Context, And Clinical Insight Into A Cohesive Journey Through The History Of Heredity. The Experience Is Immersive And Accessible, Inviting Readers To Follow Ideas As They Would A Thread Through Time. Whether You’Re New To Genetics Or Revisiting Its Milestones, The Gene Presents Key Concepts—Heredity, Dna, Chromosomes, Mutations, And Evolution—In Clear, Memorable Terms. The Book Balances Scientific Precision With Personal Reflections On Family Life And Mental Illness, Grounding Abstract Ideas In Human Experience And Moral Questions. The Pace Is Thoughtful, The Prose Engaging, And The Narrative Invites You To Consider How Scientific Progress Influences Our Sense Of Self And Responsibility In A Changing World. Comprehensive History Of Genetics From Its Earliest Ideas To Modern Science Profiles Of Central Figures: Mendel, Darwin, Crick, Rosalind Franklin Clear Explanations Of Core Concepts: Heredity, Dna, Genes, Mutations, Evolution Personal Reflections Tying Science To Family Experiences With Mental Illness Narrative-Driven, Accessible Storytelling That Blends Biography With Science Thought-Provoking Questions About Free Will, Identity, And The Ethics Of Discovery After Finishing The Gene, Readers Gain A Richer Understanding Of How Genetics Shapes Daily Life And Medicine, Along With A Deeper Appreciation For The Human Stories Behind Scientific Progress. The Book Leaves You Curious, Contemplative, And Inspired To Explore The Scientific Wonders That Define What It Means To Be Human.
works.authorDescription: Siddhartha Mukherjee is an Indian physician, biologist, and author. His first book, The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer (2010), won the 2011 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction, and Guardian First Book Award, among other awards. It was listed in the "All-Time 100 Nonfiction Books" by Time magazine in 2011. He followed it with The Gene: An Intimate History (2016), which was among The New York Times 100 best books of 2016, and a finalist for the Wellcome Trust Prize and the Royal Society Prize for Science Books. He won the 2019 Lewis Thomas Prize.

works.title: Political Violence in Ancient India

works.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
works.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
works.description: This is a philosophical fiction and classic work that follows a solitary sage who descends from the mountains to share enduring wisdom about living with purpose, independence, and a fearless view of existence. The central questions explore who we are, what we can become, and how to shape a life guided by inner conviction. It speaks to thoughtful adults and students of philosophy, literature, or personal growth who crave challenging ideas presented with literary cadence. The tone is provocative yet uplifting, inviting readers to rethink assumptions and pursue a self-directed path. The reading experience blends story-led meditations with aphoristic dialogue, presenting a narrative frame that engages large questions about meaning, power, and the nature of belief. The style is distinctive for its rhythmic cadence and compact, effect-driven passages that reward contemplation and re-reading. Readers are invited to interact mentally by weighing ideas against their own experiences, and to consider how the sage’s insights might illuminate their own choices, ambitions, and sense of self. For fiction and philosophy lovers, the journey emphasizes inner exploration and the tension between solitude and society, prompting reflection on leadership, authenticity, and the courage to think independently. It serves as a philosophical companion for those wrestling with existential questions and the ethics of self-direction. Key content elements: story-led meditations, philosophical dialogues, and concise aphorisms addressing self-mastery, independence, and the will to power Learning outcomes or reader engagement: strengthens critical thinking, self-reflection, and the ability to articulate personal beliefs Writing style: lyrical, austere prose with a mythic cadence that rewards careful reading Interactive or standout features: compact chapters ideal for daily contemplation and revisiting for fresh insights After finishing, readers gain a sharpened sense of personal agency, a more independent perspective on life choices, and a curiosity that endures. The work fosters confidence in forming one’s own beliefs, nourishes ongoing inquiry, and leaves a lasting impression as a catalyst for thoughtful living.
works.authorDescription: Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche was a German philosopher and writer who started his career as a classical philologist and turned to philosophy early in his academic career. In 1869, at age 24, he was appointed Professor of Classical Philology at the University of Basel. Plagued by health problems for most of his life, he resigned from the university in 1879. He afterward lived as an independent writer, spending much of his life in relative solitude and financial insecurity while moving between Switzerland, Italy, and southern France in search of climates that might alleviate his condition, and in the following decade, he completed much of his core writing. In 1889, aged 44, he suffered a neurological collapse, and thereafter a complete loss of his mental faculties, with paralysis and vascular dementia; he lived out his remaining 11 years, first under the care of his mother, and later his sister, until his death. His works and his philosophy have fostered not only extensive scholarship but also much popular interest.

works.title: The Intelligent Investor
works.author: Benjamin Graham
works.description: The Intelligent Investor Third Edition , The - Is The Classic Guide To Smart Investing, Written By Benjamin Graham, The Father Of Value Investing. Celebrating Its 75Th Anniversary, This Edition Adds Warren Buffett’S Introduction And Jason Zweig’S Updated Commentary While Preserving The Original Wisdom. Suited For Curious Beginners And Seasoned Investors Alike, It Offers A Calm, Practical, Educational Tone That Helps Readers Navigate Markets With Confidence. Written In A Clear, Practical Voice, The Intelligent Investor Guides You Through Core Concepts Such As Intrinsic Value, Margin Of Safety, And Risk Management. The Third Edition Maintains Graham's Structured Approach And Adds Buffett's Foreword Alongside Zweig's Chapter-By-Chapter Notes, Which Illuminate How The Ideas Apply To Today's Markets Without Altering The Original Text. The Reading Experience Is Thoughtful And Approachable, Blending Timeless Principles With Modern Insights, Making Complex Ideas Feel Accessible Through Careful Explanations And Real-World Examples. Whether You Are New To Investing Or Seeking A More Disciplined Method, The Intelligent Investor Offers A Roadmap For Evaluating Stocks And Bonds, Avoiding Common Pitfalls, And Building A Resilient Strategy. works.authorDescription: Benjamin Graham was an English-American financial analyst, economist, accountant, investor and professor. He is widely known as the "father of value investing", and wrote two of the discipline's founding texts: Security Analysis (1934) with David Dodd, and The Intelligent Investor (1949). His investment philosophy stressed independent thinking, emotional detachment, and careful security analysis, emphasizing the importance of distinguishing the price of a stock from the value of its underlying business.

works.authorDescription: Robert Morris Sapolsky (born April 6, 1957) is an American academic, neuroscientist, and primatologist. He is the John A. and Cynthia Fry Gunn Professor at Stanford University, where he is also a professor of biology, neurology, and neurosurgery. Sapolsky's research has focused on neuroendocrinology, particularly relating to stress. He is also a research associate with the National Museums of Kenya.

works.title: Indira Gandhi: A Biography
works.author: Pupul Jayakar
works.description: J.Krishnamurti A Biography Revisits The Life And Teachings Of One Of The 20Th Century's Most Influential Spiritual Teachers. This Revised, Updated Biography By Pupul Jayakar Blends Intimate Access With Historical Context To Explore Krishnamurti's Remarkable Journey—From A Child Prodigy Proclaimed The World Teacher To A Solitary Seeker Who Ultimately Dissolved The Order He Led. Written For Readers Drawn To Spirituality, Philosophy, And Self-Discovery, This Book Carries A Thoughtful, Probing, And Hopeful Tone. Crafted With The Warmth Of An Insider Account, The Narrative Weaves Conversations, Letters, And Vivid Scenes To Trace Krishnamurti's Evolving Philosophy. In J.Krishnamurti A Biography, The Book Places His Ideas In The Context Of His Era—The Theosophical Society, Annie Besant's Influence, And The Moment He Chose To Dissolve The Order And Pursue Direct Inquiry. The Biography Reveals How Personal Conviction Met Immense Questions, Making The Journey As Compelling As The Ideas Themselves. Pupul Jayakar Delivers Not Only A Chronology But A Living Portrait—Exploring The Man Behind The Teachings, The Conflicts And Commitments, And The Pursuit Of Truth Without Tradition. The Writing Is Clear And Accessible, With Thoughtful Reflections That Invite Readers To Consider Their Own Beliefs And The Nature Of Freedom. Whether You Are Encountering Krishnamurti For The First Time Or Revisiting His Teachings, The Biography Offers Insight, Inspiration, And A Spark Of Intellectual And Spiritual Curiosity. Insider Portrait Of Krishnamurti’S Life And Philosophy Detailed Look At Early World-Teacher Designation And Later Dissolution Of The Order Insights Into His Relationships, Especially With Annie Besant Clear, Engaging Narrative With Historical Context Key Themes: Truth, Freedom Of Thought, Self-Inquiry Accessible Writing That Invites Reflection And Discussion After Finishing J.Krishnamurti A Biography, Readers Gain A Nuanced Understanding Of A Man Who Challenged Conventional Boundaries—And Are Invited To Carry That Spirit Of Inquiry Into Their Own Lives, Long After The Last Page Is Turned.
works.authorDescription:
Pupul Jayakar (née Mehta; 11 September 1915 – 29 March 1997) was an Indian cultural activist and writer, best known for her work on the revival of traditional and village arts, handlooms, and handicrafts in post-independence India. According to The New York Times, she was known as "India's 'czarina of culture'", and founded arts festivals that promoted Indian arts in France, Japan, and the United States. She was a friend and biographer to both the Nehru-Gandhi family and J Krishnamurti. Jayakar had a close relationship with three prime ministers: Jawaharlal Nehru, his daughter Indira Gandhi and her son Rajiv Gandhi, and she was a close friend of Indira Gandhi. She served as cultural adviser to the latter two, confirming her preeminence in cultural matters.
In 1950, Jawaharlal Nehru invited her to study the handloom sector and work out plans for its revival. Eventually she served as chair of the All-India Handloom Board and Handicrafts and Handlooms Export Corporation and played an impo...

works.title: On the Shoulders of Giants
works.author: Stephen Hawking
works.description: On the Shoulders of Giants: The Great Works of Physics and Astronomy is a compilation of scientific texts edited and with commentary by the British theoretical physicist Stephen Hawking. The book was published by Running Press in 2002. The book contains the full text of the works of Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler, Newton, and Einstein.
works.authorDescription:
Stephen William Hawking (8 January 1942 – 14 March 2018) was an English theoretical astrophysicist, cosmologist, and author who was director of research at the Centre for Theoretical Cosmology at the University of Cambridge. Between 1979 and 2009, he was the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge, widely viewed as one of the most prestigious academic posts in the world.
Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians. In 1959, at the age of 17, he began his university education at University College, Oxford, where he received a first-class BA degree in physics. In 1962, he began his graduate work at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, where, in 1966, he obtained his PhD in applied mathematics and theoretical physics, specialising in general relativity and cosmology. In 1963, at age 21, Hawking was diagnosed with an early-onset slow-progressing form of motor neurone disease that gradually, over decades, paralysed him. After the loss of his speech, he communicated through a speech-ge...

works.title: Sikhon ka Itihas (2 parts)
